“Qui vos estis?”, inquit, responsum invicem, “Romani gentium domini.”

en: In the century after 930, Romanía conquered and annexed more territory than it ever had since the reign of Justinian (527–565), which greatly expanded the ethnic diversity of its subject population. Romanía became more like a bona fide empire—but how much?
zh: 930年之后的一百年间，罗曼尼亚征服并吞并了自查士丁尼在位（527–565）以来最多的领土，臣民的族群构成也由此大为多样。罗曼尼亚更接近一个名副其实的帝国了。接近到什么程度呢？

en: We can generally assume that people incorporated into the empire during these conquests were not Romans, whether in religion, language, or some other component of their ethnicity. To be sure, some of them immediately began the process of assimilation to Romanía, though in many places this process was cut short (in the east) or could not hope to take in such large new populations (in Bulgaria). At least initially, then, the change between 930 and 1064 represents an almost pure gain in the column of empire, dramatically shifting the balance between Romans and non-Romans. This change can be seen in the maps included at the start of this volume, which identify the empire’s major ethnic populations at the two points in its history discussed in this and the previous chapter. One area taken off the map by the later eleventh century was southern Italy, where Norman aggression confined the Roman administration to a few coastal cities before expelling it altogether, from Bari, in 1071.
zh: 我们一般可以假定，在这些征服中被并入帝国的人并非罗马人，从宗教、语言或族群身份的其他方面看都是如此。诚然，他们中有些人立即开始融入罗曼尼亚，尽管在许多地方这一进程被中断（在东方），或因为新臣民太多，无法将他们悉数吸收（如在保加利亚）。因此至少起初，930年至1064年间的变化几乎完全是扩大了罗马人统治外族的范围，急剧改变了罗马人与非罗马人之间的平衡。这一变化可见于本书卷首所附地图，它们标示出帝国在其历史上两个时点的主要族群人口，即本章与上一章所讨论的那两个时点。到十一世纪后期南意大利已从罗马版图上消失，在那里，诺曼人的侵略先使罗马的统治限于几座沿海城市，1071年又把罗马人彻底逐出最后的据点巴里。

en: However, ethnic and religious difference between conquerors and the conquered is only one criterion of empire. Another is whether the ruling power relies on mechanisms of governance that enforced that difference economically, socially, or legally. The following survey will track both criteria.
zh: 然而，征服者与被征服者之间的族群与宗教差异只是帝国的一个判准。另一个判准是统治者是否用制度在经济、社会或法律上强制维持这种差别。下面的考察将以这两个判准考察各地。

en: Empire in the Balkans
zh: 巴尔干的帝国

en: In conquering the Bulgarian empire, Romanía also inherited its diverse subject populations that lived south of the Danube and east of Duklja and Serbia. Before discussing them, it is worth noting that the Bulgarian empire may well have included a Roman population. Its cis-Danubian territories were, after all, former Roman provinces, conquered in the seventh century, and the rulers of Bulgaria frequently carried off groups of captives from Romanía and resettled them in their own lands. Some were ransomed, others not,
and defections went in both directions.
In the early tenth century, the Bulgarian ruler Simeon (893–927) began to insist on titular parity with the Roman emperor. On one of his seals he even claimed the title “
of the Romans,” albeit without mentioning there either Bulgaria or Bulgarians.

The Romans duly protested. The diplomat Theodoros Daphnopates assumed that through this title Simeon was staking a claim to rulership over a community of Romans, and asked the tsar which one he had in mind. Daphnopates assumed that it could refer only to captives of war or slaves, but it is possible that there were other Roman communities within the Bulgarian state, although probably they were small and statistically insignificant.
zh: 罗曼尼亚征服保加尔帝国时，也接收了它在多瑙河以南、杜克利亚与塞尔维亚以东的各族臣民。在讨论他们之前，值得指出的是，保加尔帝国境内很可能本来就有罗马居民。毕竟，其多瑙河以南的领土原为罗马行省，于七世纪被征服，而保加利亚的统治者经常从罗曼尼亚掳走成群的俘虏，重新安置到自己的土地上。有些人被赎回，有些则否，
也有人从一方投奔另一方，两边都有。
十世纪初，保加利亚统治者西美昂（893–927）开始要求自己的头衔同罗马皇帝对等。他在一枚印章上甚至自称“罗马人的
（国王）”，尽管印文里没有保加利亚或保加尔人的名字。
罗马人果然提出抗议。外交官狄奥多罗斯·达夫诺帕特斯认为，西美昂通过这个头衔是在主张对某个罗马人共同体的统治权，便问这位沙皇他指的是哪一个。达夫诺帕特斯认为它只能指战俘或奴隶，但保加利亚国家境内也可能存在其他罗马人共同体，尽管它们大概很小，在统计上无足轻重。

en: The majority of the population of Roman-occupied Bulgaria was likely Bulgarian, Slavic-speaking, and Orthodox (by this point, it is pointless to try to distinguish between original Bulgars and Slavs). Due to the lack of discursive narrative texts from Bulgaria, such as we have in abundance for Romanía, it is difficult to reconstruct the contours, nature, and scope of Bulgarian identity. In inscriptions, the rulers of Bulgaria juxtaposed the Bulgarians to the Romans (or “Greeks,” which is what they often called them, following western usage) and to the Magyars.

A few quasi-historical Bulgarian texts survive from the period of the Roman occupation—in reality, they are prophetic visions that garble history and eschatology—and they reveal the enduring importance of the Bulgarian state tradition and of Bulgarian peoplehood under Roman rule.
zh: 罗马占领下的保加利亚，其人口多数很可能是保加尔人、说斯拉夫语、奉正教（到这时，再试图区分原初的保加尔人与斯拉夫人已无意义）。由于缺乏来自保加利亚的能看出当事人如何理解自己身份的叙事文献（这类文本在罗曼尼亚却大量存世），很难重构保加利亚认同的轮廓、性质与范围。在铭文中，保加利亚的统治者把保加尔人与罗马人（或“希腊人”——他们常依西方用法这样称呼罗马人）以及马扎尔人并列对照。
罗马占领时期存世少量准历史的保加利亚文本——实际上它们是把历史和末世论交织在一起的预言异象——它们揭示了保加利亚国家传统与保加尔人作为一个民族的认同在罗马统治下持久的重要性。

en: For their part too, the Romans continued to regard the Bulgarians as a separate nation, a culturally inferior one to be sure, but categorically equivalent to “Roman.” Notoriously, even the Bulgarians’ conversion to Christianity did not always cause the Romans to think more highly of them. Many texts, including in religious genres, continued to depict them as a heathen or barbaric nation. An exception was Theophylaktos, their Roman-appointed archbishop at Ohrid (ca. 1100), who tried hard to find a nicer image for the majority of his flock, though even he did not think that they had become Romans.
It seems that “people like the Bulgarians, who were subjects of the empire and converts to Orthodoxy but nevertheless failed the ethnic test as Romans, were [an] anomaly.”
Religious conversion did not bridge the gap between Romans and non-Romans.
zh: 就罗马人而言，他们继续把保加尔人视为一个独立民族，固然被认为在文化上低人一等，却和“罗马人”一样属于一个独立的民族范畴。众所周知，即便保加尔人皈依基督教，也并不总使罗马人更高看他们。许多文本，包括宗教体裁的文本，继续把他们描绘为异教或野蛮民族。一个例外是塞奥菲拉克托斯，罗马任命的奥赫里德大主教（约1100年），他竭力更正面地描绘占其信众多数的这些居民，尽管连他也不认为他们已成为罗马人。
似乎“像保加尔人这样的人，虽是帝国的臣民、正教的皈依者，却在族群上却仍不够格做罗马人，倒显得有些［反常］”。
宗教皈依并未弥合罗马人与非罗马人之间的鸿沟。

en: Bulgarians could, however, assimilate to Roman norms. Basileios II, who waged a thirty-five-year war against Bulgaria, began to absorb its top men by giving them Roman offices even before he conclusively conquered their state in 1018. This process accelerated after the conquest, not only among the officer class. Soldiers were presumably recruited by the thousands into the new Roman army of the
(the regional military command) of Bulgaria.

The Bulgarian imperial family was also carted off to Constantinople and eventually married to prominent Romans; they and their descendants rose to high positions in the army, administration, and court. A striking example is provided by Aikaterine, daughter of the last Bulgarian tsar, Ivan Vladislav. In 1019, she was paraded along with the whole of her family in Basileios’ triumphal celebrations. But the husband to whom she was married off in 1025, Isaakios I Komnenos, ascended the throne thirty years later, in 1057. Aikaterine thereby became a Roman Augusta and was honored along with Isaakios in the triumphal celebration of his victories as a “joint victor.”

She had thus been both the conquered and the conqueror in a Roman triumph. I know of one precedent for this in Roman history: as a child Ventidius Bassus had been led as a captive in a triumph after the Social War, but later, as a Roman consul, he celebrated his own triumph.
zh: 然而保加尔人能够同化于罗马规范。瓦西里二世同保加尔帝国打了三十五年仗，早在1018年彻底征服其国家之前，就开始通过授予罗马官职吸纳其上层人物。这一进程在征服后加速，且不限于军官阶层。想必有数千名士兵被征入保加利亚
（doukaton，地区军事指挥部）的新罗马军队。

保加利亚皇室也被押送到君士坦丁堡，最终与显赫的罗马人联姻；他们及其后裔在军队、行政与宫廷中升至高位。一个突出的例子是末代保加利亚沙皇伊凡·弗拉迪斯拉夫之女艾卡特琳。1019年，瓦西里凯旋时，她同全家一起被带去游行示众。1025年，她被许配给伊萨克·科穆宁。约三十年后，也就是1057年，他成为皇帝伊萨克一世。艾卡特琳由此成为罗马的奥古斯塔（Augusta），并在伊萨克胜利凯旋庆典中与他一同受尊崇，被誉为“共同胜利者”。
她先后出现在两场罗马凯旋庆典上，先是被征服者，后来成了征服者。据我所知，罗马史上有一个先例：文提迪乌斯·巴苏斯幼年在同盟者战争后曾作为俘虏被引领参加凯旋式，但后来作为罗马执政官，他举行了自己的凯旋式。

en: If we ask whether occupied Bulgaria was governed in a way that reflected or maintained ethnic differences, the answer is mixed. Basileios gave court titles to Bulgarian nobles, accepted them into the Roman hierarchy, and sought “to put an end to the mutual hatred that formerly prevailed between the two peoples.”

A Roman historian, the continuator of Skylitzes, claims that Basileios “did not want to change the Bulgarians’ customs but decreed that they should live under their own rulers and manners, just as they had under Samuil.”

This can be seen in two complementary ways: as a policy of accommodation that tolerated local practices and ethnic differences, and also as a policy to maintain that difference, presumably for the benefit of the Romans. It points to a two-tiered system of administration in which Romans and Bulgarians were ruled differently, thereby replicating ethnic or former political differences.
zh: 若我们问被占领的保加利亚是否以反映或维持族群差异的方式治理，两方面都有证据。瓦西里授予保加利亚贵族宫廷头衔，接纳他们进入罗马等级体系，并寻求“终结两族之间先前盛行的相互仇恨”。
一位罗马史家，即斯基利齐斯的续编者，声称瓦西里“不想改变保加尔人的习俗，而是下令他们应由自己的首领治理，依照原有习惯生活，一如在萨穆伊尔治下”。
这可以从两种互补的角度看：既是一种容忍地方惯例与族群差异的安抚政策，也是一种维持那种差异的政策，想必是为了罗马人的利益。它指向一种双层行政体系，其中罗马人与保加尔人受不同治理，从而使族群差别或原有的政治差别得以延续。

en: However, it is unclear what “customs” and “rulers” are meant here. The only specific measure that Skylitzes mentions is the allowance that Bulgarians could continue to pay their taxes in kind rather than in coin, as they had under Samuil (the Bulgarian tsars did not mint coins). But this allowance was revoked in 1040, presumably after the Bulgarian economy had become sufficiently monetized. The change sparked a revolt.

At any rate, this fiscal concession was due to pragmatic calculations and not a desire to preserve Bulgarian customs. Occupied Bulgarians saw their economy monetized to quasi-Roman levels, transforming their relationship to the state and to each other in a more “Roman” direction. The Romans wanted more uniformity and enforced it as soon as it was possible, or even before that, judging from the revolt.
zh: 然而，这里所指的“习俗”与“统治者”究竟为何并不清楚。斯基利齐斯提到的唯一具体措施，是允许保加尔人继续像萨穆伊尔治下那样以实物而非货币纳税（保加利亚沙皇不铸币）。但这项特许于1040年撤销，想必是在保加利亚经济已充分货币化之后。这一变化引发了一场叛乱。
无论如何，这项财政让步出于务实考量，而非保存保加利亚习俗的愿望。在罗马占领下，保加利亚经济的货币化程度逐渐接近罗马，使他们与国家及彼此的关系朝更“罗马”的方向转变。罗马人想要更多一致性，只要条件允许便强制推行。从这场叛乱看，他们甚至可能动手早了些。

en: Basileios left the ecclesiastical structure of Bulgaria more or less in place, subordinating it to the archbishop of Ohrid, a position that, after a brief grace period, was given to a Roman imperial appointee.

But the organization of the Church was already the most Roman aspect of the Bulgarian empire even before the conquest; in this respect, at least, Romans and Bulgarians, who had the same faith, were on an equivalent footing. Moreover, at the level of high politics, we do not in fact find a continuation of prior Bulgarian arrangements. Bulgaria was now divided into broad spheres of Roman command (
or

), each of which encompassed a number of military themes. Basileios took over Bulgarian forts, dismantled some, and placed Roman officers in charge of the rest. The generals of the imperial army in Bulgaria were Romans, but the rank and file included Bulgarian recruits.
Those forces are called the (Roman) army of Bulgaria or sometimes “the Bulgarians.”

Military service provided Bulgarians with opportunities for advancement along with incentives to learn Roman ways. But apart from the former imperial family, which was absorbed into the upper echelons of the Roman court, we do not hear of Bulgarian officers rising high in the Roman military officer class. So Bulgarian territory was reorganized, its military was placed in the hands of Roman officers, while the locals provided mostly recruits and (likely) mid-level officers.
zh: 瓦西里大致保留了保加利亚的教会结构，使其隶属于奥赫里德大主教，短暂的过渡期后，罗马皇帝任命了该职的继任者。
但教会组织在征服前就已是保加利亚帝国最罗马化的方面；至少在这方面，拥有同一信仰的罗马人与保加尔人处于对等地位。此外，在高层政治层面，我们实际上并未发现先前保加利亚安排的延续。保加利亚如今被划分为几个幅员较广的罗马统辖区（
或
，即督军区或卡特潘军区），每个指挥区包含若干军区。瓦西里接管了保加利亚要塞，拆毁其中一些，并派罗马军官掌管其余。帝国驻保加利亚军队的将领是罗马人，但普通士兵中有从当地招入的保加尔人。
那些部队被称为（罗马的）保加利亚军队，有时也称“保加尔人”。
兵役为保加尔人提供了晋升机会，以及学习罗马方式的激励。但除了被吸纳进罗马宫廷上层的前皇室，我们史料里也再没有保加尔军官进入罗马军界高层的记载。因此保加利亚领土被重组，其军队被交到罗马军官手中，而当地人主要提供新兵与（很可能）中层军官。

en: The dismantling of the Bulgarian court would have stripped the former boyar class of much of its support, access to influence, and military power.

If Bulgarian leadership had survived the prolonged and bloody war, it was on a much reduced local level. The letters of Theophylaktos of Ohrid, written almost a century after the conquest of Bulgaria, do not give the sense that the archbishop had significant contacts among local Bulgarian notables; that stratum is almost completely absent from his network. Theophylaktos dealt primarily with Roman notables, whether in Constantinople or the provinces, and with the Bulgarian general population, not with Bulgarian elites.

While no legal mechanism was put in place to suppress the latter, the choices made by the court in political matters and in appointments to office had the same effect. If former Bulgarian elites rose high in the Roman ranks, they presumably did so under Hellenized names and it is possible that they remain invisible to us.
zh: 保加利亚宫廷的瓦解，想必剥夺了原有的波雅尔（boyar）贵族阶层所倚赖的大部分支持，使他们难以施展影响力，也削弱了他们的军权。
若保加利亚领导层在那场持久而血腥的战争后幸存下来，也只在地方上保留了少得多的势力。奥赫里德的塞奥菲拉克托斯的书信写于保加利亚被征服近一个世纪后，并未让人感觉这位大主教与当地保加利亚显贵有重要联系；他的交往中几乎没有这个阶层的人。塞奥菲拉克托斯主要与罗马显贵打交道——无论在君士坦丁堡还是行省——以及与保加利亚普通民众，而非保加利亚精英。
虽然没有设立法律机制来压制后者，但宫廷在政治事务与官职任命上的选择产生了同样效果。若前保加利亚精英在罗马等级中高升，他们想必是用了希腊化的名字，因而我们也可能认不出他们原来的身份。

en: Before the conquest, there had been little bureaucracy beneath the former Bulgarian elite, but now officers of the imperial fisc were sent out to survey the new territory so that taxes could be levied efficiently.

Over time this introduced a great deal of bureaucracy to daily life, changing the Bulgarians’ relationship to the state and making it much more Roman-like. Toward the end of the eleventh century, Theophylaktos of Ohrid was complaining in his letters about the rapaciousness of imperial tax collectors and naming all the exotic taxes that they were collecting, a typically Roman preoccupation.
His letters reveal that a complex bureaucratic apparatus was in place. One scholar has spoken of “the alignment of Bulgaria to the policies, aspirations, and tastes of Constantinople.”

We have an indirect gauge for how pervasive this was. It has been estimated that roughly three-fourths of the juridical and administrative vocabulary used in the second Bulgarian empire (formed after the rebellion of 1185) was of Roman origin, in contrast to what we know of its predecessor, conquered in 1018.
It would appear, then, that the Romans governed Bulgaria through the same fiscal mechanisms by which they governed themselves.
zh: 征服前，保加利亚精英往下几乎没有官僚体系，但现在帝国财政官员被派出去勘查新领土，以便高效征税。
随着时间推移，这许多行政程序由此进入日常生活，改变了保加尔人与国家的关系，使之更像罗马。十一世纪末，奥赫里德的塞奥菲拉克托斯在书信中抱怨帝国税吏的贪婪，并列举他们征收的所有稀奇税目——一种典型的罗马式关切。
他的书信揭示了一套复杂的官僚机器已就位。一位学者谈到“保加利亚向君士坦丁堡的政策、抱负与趣味看齐”。
间接的证据可以让我们衡量这种变化有多普遍。据估计，第二保加尔帝国（1185年起义后形成）所用司法与行政词汇约四分之三源自罗马，与其前身（1018年被征服）我们所知的情况形成对照。
因此看来，罗马人治理保加利亚，用的是他们治理自己的同一套财政机制。

en: This new bureaucracy did not hover at an elite level in a way that left the majority of the population unaffected or unconcerned. In conquered Bulgaria too, the Roman state penetrated all the way down. Consider the case of Lazar, a dependent farmer
of the Bulgarian Church, socially just a step up from being a slave. Apparently, in an effort to secure greater freedom for himself he had conspired with agents of the fisc

and accused the archbishop, Theophylaktos, of serious felony charges before no less an authority than the emperor Alexios Komnenos. Theophylaktos had to enlist his most heavyweight patrons in Constantinople to defend himself against “this Bulgarian nature that nourishes every form of evil.”

Lazar was a Bulgarian peasant, but not only was he enmeshed in the political intrigues of the provincial administration, it seems that the ancient Roman right of petitioning the emperor was available to him. Let us remember here that the founders of the second Bulgarian empire, the brothers Petar and Asen, decided to rebel when they petitioned the emperor in person for a small grant of land, were denied, and Asen was slapped across the face for speaking insolently.
This, then, was not indirect rule from a distance (“pay us
amount of taxes and we will leave you alone to manage your own affairs”). The Roman administration took on the nuts and bolts of governance at the local level.
zh: 这套新官僚体系并非只在精英层面运作，大多数民众都受其影响。在被征服的保加利亚，罗马国家也一直渗透到底层。来看拉扎尔的案例，他是保加利亚教会的一名依附农（
），社会地位仅比奴隶高一步。显然，为给自己争取更大自由，他与税务官（
）勾结，甚至直接向皇帝阿莱克修斯·科穆宁控告大主教塞奥菲拉克托斯犯有重罪。塞奥菲拉克托斯不得不求助于自己在君士坦丁堡最有权势的保护人，为自己辩护，抵御“这滋养一切邪恶的保加利亚本性”。
拉扎尔是个保加利亚农民，但他不仅卷入了行省行政的政治阴谋，似乎连古罗马向皇帝请愿的权利也对他开放。让我们在此记住，第二保加尔帝国的创立者彼得与阿森兄弟，正是在亲自向皇帝请愿求一小块封地遭拒、且阿森因出言不逊被扇耳光后，决定反叛的。
因此，这不是远距离的间接统治（“向我们缴纳
数额的税，我们就不管你们自己的事务”）。罗马官员直接介入了地方治理的具体事务。

en: The evidence of seals and the letters of Theophylaktos suggests that the Roman administration of Bulgaria was primarily military and fiscal, and less civilian, in nature. In sum, the royal family was taken off to Constantinople and broken up, the former elites were politically “decapitated,” and Bulgaria was governed by Romans through primarily military and fiscal institutions, without giving its people much opportunity to rise in the Roman system. In this sense, it looks more like an occupation, for all that Bulgarians and Romans shared the same religion and were, after the conquest, probably subject to the same laws.
zh: 印章证据与塞奥菲拉克托斯的书信表明，罗马对保加利亚的行政主要属军事与财政性质，民政所占比重较小。总之，皇室被带往君士坦丁堡并拆散，原有的精英阶层失去了政治领袖，保加利亚由罗马人通过主要属军事与财政的制度治理，当地人在罗马体制内也少有晋升的机会。在这个意义上，它更像一场占领，尽管保加尔人与罗马人共享同一宗教，且在征服后很可能受同样法律约束。

en: Therefore, some Bulgarians may have felt that they were under foreign occupation, whereas others had access to opportunities available to Romans. Yet they were not Romans, and so it was easier to say that they formed a part of the
of the Romans than their
This points to the distinction, found in some sources, between Romanía and the
of the Romans.

It is significant that Bulgarians mounted three rebellions against Constantinople, in 1040, 1072, and 1185, the last one of which succeeded. The Roman sources state that they were moved in part by a desire for national independence.

Modern scholars were for long trained to instinctively reject such motives for premodern people, but there is no reason to deny that this was at least part of the picture, supported as it is by so many sources. For resentful Bulgarians, Roman rule felt a lot more like “empire.” But there were also many times during the occupation when the Bulgarian army under Roman command remained loyal to the empire under difficult circumstances. Occupied Bulgaria therefore presents a mixed picture.
zh: 因此，有些保加尔人可能觉得自己处于外国占领之下，而另一些人则能获得罗马人可享的机会。然而他们不是罗马人，所以将他们所居之地纳入罗马
，比将他们视为罗马
的成员更容易。
这指向某些史料中罗曼尼亚与罗马人的
（统治范围）之间的区分。
意味深长的是，保加尔人发动了三次反君士坦丁堡的叛乱，分别在1040、1072与1185年，最后一次成功了。罗马史料称，他们部分出于民族独立的愿望。
现代学者长期受到一种学术训练，往往本能地否认前现代的人会有这样的动机，但没有理由否认这至少是图景的一部分，毕竟有这么多史料支持。对心怀怨恨的保加尔人而言，罗马统治感觉更像“帝国”。但在占领期间，也有许多时候罗马指挥下的保加利亚军队在艰难处境中仍对帝国保持忠诚。因此被占领的保加利亚呈现一幅复杂图景。

en: The greater level of documentation produced by the Roman state and by Roman authors immediately shed light on at least two ethnic groups that had been living in the broader Bulgarian realm but had so far remained invisible: the Albanians and the Vlachs. This is not the place to rehearse the contentious debates that surround the origin and early history of both groups, as we are interested only in their relation to the Roman state. Unfortunately, it is almost impossible to see what that was, especially in the case of the Albanians, located in the hinterland of the theme of Dyrrachion. They are mentioned for the first time in the eleventh century, as they formed ethnically distinct military units, for example, “an army of Romans, Bulgarians, and Arvanites.”

It is not known what kind of administrative presence the empire maintained in their mountainous homeland; possibly it was indirect. When Bohemond invaded the empire in 1107, some of them sided with him and showed him the mountain paths.
zh: 罗马国家与罗马作者产生的更丰富文献，立即揭示了至少两个早就生活在保加尔政权所辖的广大地区、此前却没有留下记载的族群：阿尔巴尼亚人与弗拉赫人。这里不是重述围绕这两个群体起源与早期历史的争议性辩论的地方，因为我们只关心他们与罗马国家的关系。遗憾的是，这层关系几乎无从查考，尤其对阿尔巴尼亚人而言，他们位于都拉基翁军区腹地。他们在十一世纪首次被提及，当时他们组成族群上独立的军事单位，例如“一支由罗马人、保加尔人与阿尔瓦尼特人组成的军队”。
帝国在他们的山地故乡如何施政不得而知，也许是间接治理。1107年博希蒙德入侵帝国时，他们中有些人站到他一边，给他指了山间小路。

en: The Vlachs, a mostly pastoral people who spoke a Romance language, are attested immediately in the
that Basileios II issued in 1020 to confirm the rights and jurisdiction of the former Church of Bulgaria.
Unfortunately, he does not say much about them or specify the administrative arrangements by which he intended them to be governed (ecclesiastical

were not for that). Our sources for the Vlachs under Roman rule are poor. In the 1070s, Kekaumenos wrote a manual with advice to emperors and governors, and he was personally familiar with central Greece. He claims that one of his ancestors, Nikoulitzas, who formerly held a military post in Greece, was, in 979, given the command
of the Vlachs of Greece by Basileios II.
Apparently there were Vlachs in Romanía long before the war with Bulgaria was over and they performed military service as an ethnic unit under a Roman-appointed

This arrangement was similar to that which governed the Slavs of central Greece in the seventh and eighth centuries: a quasi-autonomous ethnic group providing soldiers to the empire but not fully assimilated to its administration or cultural life.

We do not, however, know Nikoulitzas’ ethnicity, and this area of central Greece, along with Kekaumenos’ ancestors themselves, would oscillate between Bulgaria and Romanía during Basileios II’s long war.
zh: 弗拉赫人是一个主要以畜牧为生、说一种罗曼语族语言的民族，最早就见于瓦西里二世于1020年颁布、用以确认前保加利亚教会权利与管辖权的
（sigillia，帝国印章文书）中。
遗憾的是，他关于他们说得不多，也未具体说明他打算如何管辖他们（教会
不是为此而设）。我们关于罗马统治下弗拉赫人的史料很贫乏。1070年代，凯考梅诺斯写了一部给皇帝与总督献策的手册，他本人熟悉希腊中部。他声称自己的一位祖先尼库利察斯，先前在希腊担任军职，于979年被瓦西里二世授予对希腊弗拉赫人的
（arche）。
显然，早在对保加利亚战争结束之前很久，罗曼尼亚境内就有弗拉赫人，他们作为一个族群单位、在罗马任命的
（archon）之下服兵役。这一安排类似于七、八世纪治理希腊中部斯拉夫人的那种：一个半自治的族群向帝国提供兵员，却没有完全纳入其行政体系，也未完全融入其文化生活。
然而我们不知道尼库利察斯的族群性，而希腊中部这一地区，连同凯考梅诺斯的祖先本身，在瓦西里二世的漫长战争期间在保加利亚与罗曼尼亚之间反复转归。

en: The next window opens in 1066. Kekaumenos gives a detailed account of a rebellion that took place in Thessaly in 1066 that involved the people of Larissa along with some Vlachs and Bulgarians, who were all protesting a tax hike. The (reluctant) leader of the rebellion was one Nikoulitzas Delphinas, a descendant of the

of the Vlachs in 979, which may have been part of the reason why the Vlachs now turned to him. Nikoulitzas Delphinas was related by marriage to Kekaumenos and was the source for the account that he gives of the events. He presents the Vlachs as pastoralists who moved their flocks between Thessaly and the former territory of the Bulgarian empire, but they also maintained a presence in the towns of Thessaly.

Kekaumenos’ accounts of their activities and lifestyle makes it seem that they were not entirely under the control of imperial authority, but they were planning an armed rebellion and showed up ready to fight, so they must have had some kind of military organization. It appears that they no longer had a separate
appointed by the emperor.
Kekaumenos follows his account of the rebellion with a brief ethnography of the Vlachs. He calls them a faithless and perverse
that is not to be trusted. He advises governors to secure the Vlachs’ wives and children in “the cities of Romanía” as hostages to their good behavior.
zh: 再有具体记载已是1066年。凯考梅诺斯详细记述了1066年发生在色萨利的一场叛乱，卷入者包括拉里萨人以及一些弗拉赫人与保加尔人，他们都在抗议增税。这场叛乱的（不情愿的）领袖是一位尼库利察斯·德尔菲纳斯，即979年弗拉赫人
（archon）的后裔，这或许正是弗拉赫人如今转向他的部分原因。尼库利察斯·德尔菲纳斯与凯考梅诺斯有姻亲关系，这段叛乱经过，凯考梅诺斯就是听他说的。他把弗拉赫人呈现为在色萨利与前保加利亚帝国领土之间赶牲畜转场的牧民，同时也有人常驻色萨利的城镇。
凯考梅诺斯对他们活动与生活方式的记述，让人觉得他们并非完全处于帝国权威控制之下，但他们当时正策划一场武装叛乱，而且集结时已准备参战，所以他们想必有某种军事组织。似乎他们不再有一位由皇帝任命的独立
（archon）。
凯考梅诺斯在叛乱记述之后附了一小段弗拉赫人民族志。他称他们为一个不可信任的、背信而乖张的
（genos）。他建议总督们把弗拉赫人的妻儿扣在“罗曼尼亚诸城”作为人质，使他们不敢反叛。

en: A mobile group of Vlach pastoralists was known as a

In the early twelfth century, one such group, consisting of three hundred families, had settled near Mt. Athos, causing a headache to imperial authorities for reasons that we need not get into here. One of the documents generated by their presence claims that the emperor Alexios I Komnenos was basically treating a
as a taxable unit equivalent to a Roman
(or village, a fiscal unit).

This is one way in which the Roman authorities tried to place the Vlachs under familiar rubrics. Later in the twelfth century Anna Komnene noted that the Vlachs had their own villages but lived a nomadic life; the Roman army once mistook them for Cumans.
All this suggests both ethnic alterity and quasi-autonomy. The Vlachs are mentioned repeatedly as a source of soldiers, probably as ethnic auxiliaries.

In 1162, the Jewish traveler Benjamin of Tudela says that the Vlachs come down from the mountains of central Greece to rob and pillage, and no state authority resists them; the emperors have failed to tame them. He hyperbolically added that “they do not even profess the Christian faith.”
A twelfth-century governor of Greece was praised for waging war against the “outlandish barbarians who live in the most inaccessible mountains of Greece, who are highway robbers and tax-evaders.”

The Vlachs of Thessaly, then, along probably with the Vlachs in many parts of the former Bulgarian empire, were not fully “pacified,” to use an ancient Roman term. They occupied the gray area between the polity and the empire of the Romans, and were not even fully subject to the latter. Even before 1204, mountainous Thessaly was being called Vlachia.
zh: 弗拉赫牧民的一个流动群体被称为
（katouna）。十二世纪初，一个由三百户家庭组成的这类群体定居在阿索斯山附近，因一些我们在此不必深究的原因令帝国当局头疼。他们的存在所产生的文书之一声称，皇帝阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁基本上把一个
当作相当于罗马
（即村庄，一个财政单位）的纳税单位。
这是罗马当局试图按现行的税籍分类管辖弗拉赫人的一种方式。十二世纪稍后，安娜·科穆宁娜指出，弗拉赫人有自己的村庄，却过游牧生活；罗马军队曾把他们误认为库曼人。
所有这些都暗示他们有别于罗马人，同时享有一定的自治。弗拉赫人屡次被记作兵员来源，很可能编为外族辅助部队。
1162年，犹太旅行家图德拉的便雅悯说，弗拉赫人从希腊中部山区下来抢劫掠夺，没有任何国家权威抵抗他们；皇帝们未能驯服他们。他夸张地补充说“他们甚至不信奉基督教信仰”。
一位十二世纪的希腊总督因对“住在希腊最难以进入山区的异族蛮人——他们是拦路抢劫者与逃税者”作战而受赞扬。
因此，色萨利的弗拉赫人，很可能连同前保加利亚帝国许多地区的弗拉赫人，用一个古罗马术语来说，并未被完全“平定”。他们占据罗马人政治共同体与帝国之间的灰色地带，甚至不完全臣属于后者。早在1204年之前，多山的色萨利就已被称为弗拉基亚。

en: Even though they were orthodox, in some contexts Vlachs from the mountains could be regarded as essentially different from the Romans. We have scant information about this, but it is suggestive of systemic discrimination on ethnic grounds. In the early thirteenth century, the bishop of Naupaktos, Ioannes Apokaukos, granted a divorce and cited, among other reasons, the fact that the wife was “a barbarian and did not speak Greek correctly”—he says this twice in his ruling—adding that she was from the mountainous regions of Velahatouïa and was accordingly given the baptismal name Rousa, an ethnic association that he assumed his readers would understand. She may have been a Vlach or a Slav—we do not know—but we have here a Roman bishop dissolving an orthodox marriage in part because of the couple’s ethnic differences, along with their great age difference. On all these grounds, he deemed it “absurd” that they had been married in the first place.
zh: 尽管他们是正教徒，在某些语境下，来自山区的弗拉赫人仍可能被视为本质上不同于罗马人。这方面材料很少，却使人想到族群歧视也可能成为常规。十三世纪初，纳夫帕克托斯主教约安尼斯·阿波卡夫科斯批准了一桩离婚，援引的理由之一是妻子“是个蛮族，且讲不好希腊语”——他在裁决中两次这样说——并补充说她来自韦拉哈图亚的山区，因而被赋予洗礼名鲁萨，他显然以为读者知道这个名字同哪一族有关。她可能是弗拉赫人或斯拉夫人——我们不知道——但我们在此看到一位罗马主教部分因夫妻的族群差异、外加巨大的年龄差异而解除一桩正教婚姻。基于所有这些理由，他认为他们当初结婚本就是“荒谬的”。

en: Immediately after the Vlachs, Basileios’

refers to the Turks of the Vardar valley (i.e., the Axios). These were probably Hungarian mercenaries who were hired and settled there, north of Thessalonike, either by Samuil or Basileios himself. By the eleventh century they had their own bishop. The unit, with the same ethnogeographical name, is attested in the later Byzantine period, but by then its ethnic composition had changed; it is likely that only the original name remained, linked to the place or to the unit recruited from it.
zh: 紧接弗拉赫人之后，瓦西里的
（sigillion）提到瓦尔达尔河谷（即阿克西奥斯河）的突厥人。他们很可能是被雇佣并安置在那里（塞萨洛尼基以北）的匈牙利雇佣兵，雇佣者或是萨穆伊尔，或是瓦西里本人。到十一世纪他们有了自己的主教。这个用同一个兼指族群和地名的名称称呼的部队，在拜占庭晚期仍有记载，但那时其族群构成已改变；旧名可能只是沿用于这一地方，或用于从这里招募的部队。

en: Moving our focus to Thrace, the emperor Ioannes I Tzimiskes moved many Paulicians from the eastern frontier to Philippopolis in Thrace, to guard the passes there. These Paulicians were presumably incorporated by the empire in its recent conquests in the east, as the request for their transfer came from the new Byzantine bishop of Antioch. One century later, these Paulicians were still in Philippopolis, forming a large part of the local population and providing soldiers to the empire. Alexios Komnenos converted many of them to Orthodoxy, after which they are rarely mentioned.
A smaller community of Paulicians or Bogomils was destroyed by Bohemond at Pelagonia in 1097, when his contingent of the First Crusade marched across the Balkans.
zh: 把焦点移到色雷斯，皇帝约安尼斯一世·齐米斯凯斯把许多保罗派从东部边疆迁到色雷斯的菲利波波利斯，守卫那里的关隘。这些保罗派想必是在帝国最近征服东方领地时才成为罗马臣民的，因为迁移他们的请求来自安条克的新拜占庭主教。一个世纪后，这些保罗派仍在菲利波波利斯，占当地人口相当大的比例，并为帝国提供士兵。阿莱克修斯·科穆宁使他们中许多人皈依正教，此后他们便很少被提及。
1097年，一个较小的保罗派或鲍格米勒派社群在佩拉戈尼亚被博希蒙德摧毁，当时他那支第一次十字军东征的分队正穿过巴尔干。

en: Finally, the lower Danube delta, the corner of imperial territory where the river met the Black Sea, was occupied by Pechenegs. Two groups of them had entered the empire in the late 1040s. Konstantinos IX Monomachos had tried to settle both groups on imperial territory and recruit them into the army, but it went horribly wrong. After years of fighting, the two sides came to an agreement: the Pechenegs would recognize the emperor but remain mostly autonomous. For the Romans, the Pechenegs were nomadic Scythians, as far from being civilized Romans as possible, and even after the agreement they occasionally raided the Roman provinces when the Romans were preoccupied, for example during civil wars.

As they were not settled in predominantly Roman lands, despite their nominal conversion to Orthodoxy there was no question of their assimilation. Moreover, they had entered with their own women and children and were not successfully dispersed (though that had been the original plan). So the Pechenegs ended up forming an ethnic enclave; in fact, it is not clear that we should treat them as part of the empire. Kekaumenos, who wrote a book with advice in the 1070s, warned against such experiments: “If the enemy asks you to cede part of your territory to him, do not agree unless he agrees to be subject to you and pay you taxes, and even then do it only in great need. The Romans have suffered many disasters from such things . . . for example, the Pechenegs entered Romanía in this way.”

The Pechenegs were finally crushed by Alexios Komnenos at the battle of Lebounion in 1091, after which they were incorporated into the imperial army. In this capacity, they served the empire well, albeit in smaller dispersed units.
zh: 最后，多瑙河下游三角洲，即河流与黑海交汇的帝国领土一角，为佩切涅格人所占据。他们中两群人在1040年代后期进入帝国。君士坦丁九世·莫诺马霍斯曾试图把两群人都安置在帝国领土上并征入军队，但这项安排结果适得其反。经过多年战斗，双方达成协议：佩切涅格人承认皇帝，但基本保持自治。对罗马人而言，佩切涅格人是游牧的斯基泰人，同自视文明的罗马人迥然有别，即便协议之后，他们仍偶尔趁罗马人无暇他顾（例如内战期间）袭扰罗马行省。

由于他们未被安置在以罗马人为主的土地上，尽管名义上皈依正教，却谈不上同化。此外，他们是携家眷一同来的，原先将他们分散安置的计划并未实现（尽管那本是原计划）。于是佩切涅格人最终形成一个族群飞地；事实上，我们是否应把他们当作帝国的一部分并不清楚。凯考梅诺斯在1070年代写了一本献策之书，提醒统治者不要轻易作此尝试：“若敌人要求你把部分领土割让给他，不要同意，除非他同意臣属于你并向你纳税，而即便如此，也只在万不得已时才这样做。罗马人因这类事遭受过许多灾难……例如，佩切涅格人就是这样进入罗曼尼亚的。”
佩切涅格人最终于1091年在莱布尼翁战役被阿莱克修斯·科穆宁击溃，此后他们被并入帝国军队。他们此后编为较小的部队，分驻各地，为帝国效力颇为得力。

en: New Armenian Subjects
zh: 新的亚美尼亚臣民

en: Turning to the east, the largest non-Roman ethnicity absorbed by the empire in its expansion were the Armenians. The empire annexed the realm of Taron around 968 (it was voluntarily ceded by its ruler); then a portion of the mixed Georgian-Armenian realm of Upper Tao in 1000 (its ruler had backed the wrong side in a Roman civil war in the 980s and had to bequeath part of his state to Rome in his will); Vaspurakan around 1020 (voluntarily ceded); Ani in 1045 (its ruler had also backed the wrong side in the war of 1022 and had to bequeath his realm, but its annexation was resisted when he died); and Vanand (Kars) in 1064 / 5 (voluntarily ceded while the Seljuks were conquering the Caucasus). The majority of Armenians thereby became imperial subjects, albeit briefly: the most important of the former principalities were held by the empire for fifty years (Vaspurakan), twenty (Ani), and a handful (Vanand). This constricts our ability to see how the empire governed them. The window narrows even more if we assume, as we must, that local practices were generally left in place and changes made only gradually, as in Bulgaria.
zh: 转向东方，帝国扩张中吸纳的最大非罗马族群是亚美尼亚人。帝国约968年吞并塔隆王国（由其统治者自愿割让）；接着1000年吞并格鲁吉亚人和亚美尼亚人混居的上陶王国的一部分（其统治者在980年代一场罗马内战中站错了队，不得不立下遗嘱，将一部分领土交给罗马）；约1020年的瓦斯普拉坎（自愿割让）；1045年的阿尼（其统治者也在1022年战争中站错了队，不得不遗赠其王国，但他死后吞并遭到抵抗）；以及1064或1065年的瓦南德（卡尔斯）（在塞尔柱人征服高加索时自愿割让）。亚美尼亚人由此多数成为帝国臣民，尽管为时短暂：几个最重要的原公国中，瓦斯普拉坎由帝国统治了五十年，阿尼二十年，瓦南德仅有几年。这限制了我们看清帝国如何治理他们的能力。若我们假定（而我们必须这样假定）地方惯例一般被保留、变化只逐步发生，如在保加利亚那样，就更难从这段短暂时期看清帝国统治的实际情形。

en: It was not only in the annexed principalities that Armenians could be found in the empire. Roman expansion into the Caucasus had been preceded in the tenth century by a push against the Muslim emirates of Cilicia, Syria, Melitene, and Mesopotamia. As it annexed territories there, in the southeast, the empire established many smaller frontier themes that were manned largely by Armenian soldier-settlers. Melias had pioneered these when he founded the fort theme of Lykandos. These relatively short-lived formations came to be known as the smaller “Armenian themes” that were juxtaposed to the older “large Roman themes.”
In the second half of the tenth century, therefore, Armenians began to play a more prominent role in the imperial army,
which was expanding and in need of manpower, although prejudices against their reliability persisted on the Roman side.
“Roman” and “Armenian” soldiers are juxtaposed in narrative accounts of operations composed by both Roman and Arab writers.

Beyond the empire’s reliance on Armenian frontiersmen, its settlement of Armenians in an arc from the Caucasus to the Mediterranean initiated a population drift from Armenia, which later enabled the formation of Armenian states in Cilicia, among other places.
zh: 帝国内能找到亚美尼亚人的地方不限于被吞并的诸公国。十世纪罗马向高加索的扩张之前，罗马军队先向基利家、叙利亚、梅利泰内及美索不达米亚的穆斯林埃米尔国推进。随着帝国吞并那里（东南部）的领土，它设立了许多较小的边疆军区，驻守者大多是就地定居的亚美尼亚士兵。梅利亚斯创立利坎多斯要塞军区时开了先河。这类建制存续不久被称为较小的“亚美尼亚军区”，与较旧的“大罗马军区”并列对照。
因此十世纪后半叶，亚美尼亚人开始在帝国军队中扮演更突出的角色，
军队当时正在扩张、需要人力，尽管罗马方面仍有成见，认为他们靠不住。
在罗马与阿拉伯作者撰写的作战叙事记载中，“罗马”士兵与“亚美尼亚”士兵被并列对照。
除了帝国倚重亚美尼亚边民，它把亚美尼亚人安置在从高加索到地中海的弧形地带，促使亚美尼亚人口逐渐迁入这些地方，这后来促成了基利家等地亚美尼亚国家的形成。

en: How did the empire govern Armenians? In sum, Roman policy toward them was not much different from its policy toward the Bulgarians, despite the different ways in which Armenian territories were acquired and the confessional split between the Byzantine and Armenian Churches. The new territories—both the smaller Armenian themes and the annexed principalities—were grouped into broader military commands under a
or
who was usually a Roman career officer.

The armies beneath him, by contrast, led by the regional generals, were probably recruited to a considerable degree among the local population. Unfortunately, we know little about the administrative structures that were put in place in Armenia. Narrative notices are few. The Armenian historian Aristakes says that when Basileios II annexed part of Tao he appointed “officials, judges and overseers” in the forts and the cities there.

Later in his narrative, Aristakes twice records “judges” being sent out from Constantinople to Iberia and Taron, where they adjudicated local disputes; we sorely want to know by what laws they governed.

From lead seals we know that men were posted to all the top positions in the Roman administration, both military and civilianjudicial, that we can expect to have left a record. This was true in both the small Armenian themes and the big regional commands formed out of the former principalities, suggesting that the empire intended to install the full apparatus of governance that it used in the Roman themes, just as it did in Bulgaria. These officials were a mix of Romans and locals.
zh: 帝国如何治理亚美尼亚人？总之，罗马对他们的政策与对保加尔人的政策没有太大不同，尽管亚美尼亚领土的获取方式不同，且拜占庭与亚美尼亚教会之间存在教派分裂。新领土——较小的亚美尼亚军区与被吞并的诸公国——被归入更大的军事指挥部，由一名
（doux）或
（katepano）统领，担任这些职位的通常是罗马职业军官。
相比之下，他麾下由地区将领统率的军队，很可能有相当一部分是在当地征募的。遗憾的是，我们对亚美尼亚设立的行政结构知之甚少。叙事史料鲜有记载。亚美尼亚史家阿里斯塔克斯说，瓦西里二世吞并陶的一部分时，在那里的要塞与城市任命了“官员、法官与监督者”。
在其叙事后面，阿里斯塔克斯两次记载“法官”从君士坦丁堡被派往伊比利亚与塔隆，在那里裁决地方纠纷；我们极想知道他们依何种法律治理。
从铅印我们得知，罗马行政中所有可望留下记录的最高职位——军事与民政司法——均有任命记录。这在较小的亚美尼亚军区与由前诸公国组成的大地区指挥部皆然，表明帝国意在部署罗马军区所用的整套行政制度，正如它在保加利亚所做。官员中既有罗马人，也有当地人。

en: Like the former Bulgarian empire, the former Armenian principalities had not minted coins. To the degree that their economies were monetized, they had relied on Roman and Muslim coinage. The Roman presence would have increased monetization, if only because of the influx of pay given to the soldiers and officers stationed in the new commands, but we do not know how this intersected with tax policy. I have found no studies of the monetization of the local economies during this period, though thousands of Byzantine coins have been discovered.
Aristakes refers in one place to a tax official sent from Constantinople and elsewhere records the court’s desire to tax the Armenian Church, a plan that was abandoned.

But he does not say what form these taxes took (or would have taken). Two imperial governors of Ani posted inscriptions that reveal that the city, if not its surrounding territory, had been regimented by a full apparatus of requisitions, taxes, corves on labor, and exemptions; these typically Roman administrative and fiscal arrangements had no counterpart in the former Armenian royal tradition. To display this new order prominently in the minds of locals, the governors had the inscriptions carved outside the public door of the cathedral of Ani.

Unfortunately, we do not know how deeply the Roman bureaucracy penetrated into the newly acquired territories around the city in the two decades that it controlled them. In general, it would be safest to assume that local norms continued in force outside the context of the army and the higher levels of political power, with the additional caveat that the nature of elite society and the ideology projected by politicized spaces was significantly transformed.
zh: 与原保加尔帝国一样，前亚美尼亚诸公国不铸币。经济活动中凡是用到货币的地方，都靠罗马或穆斯林的钱币。罗马的存在想必增加了货币化，哪怕只因驻新指挥部士兵与军官的军饷流入，但我们不知道这与税收政策如何交织。我未找到关于这一时期地方经济货币化的研究，尽管已发现数千枚拜占庭钱币。
阿里斯塔克斯在一处提到从君士坦丁堡派来的税务官员，在别处记载宫廷想对亚美尼亚教会征税的计划，该计划被放弃。
但他没说这些税采取（或本会采取）何种形式。阿尼的两任帝国总督张贴铭文，揭示该城（即便不含其周边领土）已按一整套关于征用、纳税、服劳役及豁免的制度加以治理；这些典型的罗马行政与财政安排，在前亚美尼亚王室传统中没有对应物。为了让当地人都看到这套新制度，总督们命人把铭文刻在阿尼大教堂公共大门外。
遗憾的是，我们不知道在帝国控制该城周边新获领土的二十年间，罗马官僚体系渗透有多深。一般而言，最稳妥的假定是：在军队与政治权力高层之外，地方规范继续有效，但须附加一点提醒：精英社会的性质与公共权力场所所宣示的观念已显著转变。

en: As in Bulgaria, the bureaucratization of the armed forces undermined the power of Armenian aristocrats, the “feudal” lords of the former principalities, some of whom had been required to give up their lands and forts. This by itself had massive effects on local society. The former nobility could preserve their high status by seeking positions in the Roman army and administration, but that would have embedded them further in the Roman order. Any doubts that a new and different power was now in charge would have been lain to rest when Basileios II established an army of Bulgarians in Vaspurakan;

Varangians and Franks were soon to follow. Most forts, at least initially, were placed in the hands of Roman officers. In the early 1050s, Konstantinos IX Monomachos sent a fiscal official to reorganize the armies of Iberia and possibly Mesopotamia, altering previous arrangements regarding funding, land, and service. This reform was regarded as disastrous at the time and has a notorious reputation in scholarship, even though its nature remains opaque. Whatever it was, it seems to have rested on typical Roman technologies of administration, including registers of lands, soldiers, and payments to and by the state. These probably introduced to the east practices that were being used in the core territories of the empire.
zh: 如在保加利亚，军队的官僚化削弱了亚美尼亚贵族的权力，即前诸公国的“封建”领主，他们中有些人被要求放弃土地与要塞。仅此一点就对地方社会产生巨大影响。前贵族可通过在罗马军队与行政中谋职保持高地位，但那会使他们更深嵌入罗马秩序。当瓦西里二世在瓦斯普拉坎建立一支保加尔人军队时，当地人便已不难断定，这里确实换了统治者；

瓦良格人与法兰克人不久也将到来。至少要塞起初大多交到罗马军官手中。1050年代初，君士坦丁九世·莫诺马霍斯派一名财政官员重组伊比利亚的军队，可能还重组了美索不达米亚的军队，改变了先前关于经费、土地与服役的安排。这场改革当时被视为灾难性的，在学界声名狼藉，尽管其性质仍晦暗不明。无论它是什么，似乎都依托典型的罗马行政技术，如登记土地、兵员及国家收付款项的册簿。这些很可能把帝国核心领土正在使用的做法引入了东方。

en: The empire also established many Chalcedonian ecclesiastical sees in the new territories to match those of the (anti-Chalcedonian) Armenian Church; a minority of Armenians were already Chalcedonian and a number switched at this time.
But the Armenian Church also began, in the 960s or 970s, to establish its own sees inside imperial territory, especially in Syria but also at Sebasteia.

For the first time in over three hundred years, a significant presence of non-Chalcedonian Christians was felt within the empire. The eleventh century did witness a rise in Orthodox polemics against Armenian Christianity, attacks that were, through complicated channels that we need not explore here, caught up in the emerging schism between Rome and Constantinople.
But the emperors did not persecute the Armenian Church, as they did, at times, the Syrian Church (see below).

Instead, the authorities took a more pragmatic approach. An attack against Armenian priests instigated by the bishop of Sebasteia is reported for 986–987, but the emperor put a quick stop to it—if we can believe the report.
After the annexation of Ani (in ca. 1045), the Armenian

(chief prelate) Petros was removed to Constantinople before being relocated to Asia Minor. But these movements may not have been forced, and he seems to have received rock star treatment in the capital.
More importantly, we know of a number of non-Chalcedonian Armenians who were appointed to high offices and given court titles.
zh: 帝国还在新领土设立了许多卡尔西顿派教会主教区，与（反对卡尔西顿会议的）亚美尼亚教会各主教区相对应；少数亚美尼亚人本已是卡尔西顿派，还有一些在此时改宗。
但亚美尼亚教会也在960或970年代开始在帝国境内设立自己的主教区，尤其在叙利亚，也在塞巴斯泰亚。
帝国三百多年来第一次有了人数颇多的非卡尔西顿派基督徒。十一世纪确实见证了正教针对亚美尼亚基督教的论战增多，这些攻击通过我们在此不必探究的复杂渠道，又与罗马和君士坦丁堡两教会逐渐形成的裂痕纠缠在一起。
但皇帝们并未迫害亚美尼亚教会，不像他们有时对叙利亚教会那样（见下文）。
相反，当局采取更务实的做法。据报986–987年塞巴斯泰亚主教煽动了一场针对亚美尼亚司铎的攻击，但皇帝迅速制止了它——如果我们可以相信这则报道。
阿尼被吞并后（约1045年），亚美尼亚
（katholikos，首席主教）彼得罗斯被迁到君士坦丁堡，随后又被安置到小亚细亚。但这些迁移未必是强制的，而且他在首都似乎备受礼遇，俨然一位万众瞩目的人物。
更重要的是，我们知道有一些非卡尔西顿派亚美尼亚人被任命担任高级官职并获授宫廷头衔。

en: Thus, while there is abundant evidence for ethnic difference and even for virulent expressions of prejudice between Romans and Armenians, there is no evidence for an overt or systematic politics of difference in the empire’s rule over Armenians. The latter could rise in the hierarchy, and many did so. Toward the end of the eleventh century, when the Roman east collapsed, its fragments fell into the hands of officers such as Philaretos Brachamios, Gabriel of Melitene, and Theodoros of Edessa, all of whom the sources call both Armenian and Roman in alternating ways or in various combinations. These figures, who are cherished today for being so complex and ambiguous in their identity,

were the product of an unfinished assimilation of local Armenian officers. In better times, they would have advanced their careers by going to the capital, intermarrying with the Roman elite, and being posted to non-Armenian provinces. That path, as we have seen, had been followed by many Armenian nobles in previous centuries and, in the later tenth century, by the rulers of Taron, who went on to become the Taronites, a Roman family that joined the Komnenian aristocracy.

But those options were blocked by the fall of Asia Minor to the Turks, which cut these lands off from Constantinople and opened up other, more local opportunities for personal self-aggrandizement in the post-Roman east.
zh: 因此，尽管有大量证据表明罗马人与亚美尼亚人之间的族群差异、甚至恶毒的偏见表达，却没有证据表明帝国对亚美尼亚人的统治中存在公开或系统性的差异政治。亚美尼亚人能够在等级体系中上升，许多人也确实如此。十一世纪末，当罗马东方崩溃时，昔日的领地分由菲拉雷托斯·布拉哈米奥斯、梅利泰内的加布里埃尔、埃德萨的狄奥多罗斯等军官控制。史料有时称他们为亚美尼亚人，有时称他们为罗马人，也有将两个名称合用的时候。这些人物如今因其认同如此复杂暧昧而受珍视，
反映了当地亚美尼亚军官尚未完成的同化过程。在较好的时代，他们本会通过前往首都、与罗马上层联姻、被派驻非亚美尼亚行省来推进仕途。如我们所见，那条路径在前几个世纪已被许多亚美尼亚贵族走过，十世纪后期也被塔隆的统治者走过，他们后来成为塔隆尼特斯家族，一个加入科穆宁贵族的罗马家族。
但那些选择被小亚细亚落入突厥人之手所阻断，这使这些土地与君士坦丁堡隔绝，并在后罗马时代的东方开启了另一些在地方上扩张个人权势的机会。

en: This brings us to the major demographic shift experienced by the Roman east during the eleventh century: a migration of Armenians who moved from their annexed principalities into Cappadocia, Cilicia, and Syria. This move was facilitated by the empire’s expansion but likely caused by the Turkish raids into the Caucasus and the increasing instability of the area. Armenian military themes had already been established in an arc down the Caucasus to Cilicia, but there was one more vector of migration: the transfer of the former royal families to Roman Cappadocia. One chronicle, simplifying considerably, directly links the migration of Armenians to the transplantation of their royal families.

But that transplantation has been described in misleading terms by some scholars. As it concerns the mechanisms by which Romanía managed its ethnic minorities, a word must be said about it. According to a “maximalist” interpretation of the transfer of the royalty of Vaspurakan, Ani, and Kars, the royals were granted largely autonomous ethnic Armenian “principalities” within Cappadocia, principalities that were both massive in size and hereditary and that they ruled with the feudal armies that they brought from Armenia. They even conducted their own “foreign policy,” sometimes against the empire itself.
zh: 这就涉及十一世纪罗马帝国东部人口构成的一次重大变化：亚美尼亚人从被吞并的诸公国迁往卡帕多基亚、基利家与叙利亚。这一迁移由帝国扩张促成，但很可能由突厥人对高加索的袭扰及该地区日益加剧的不稳定所引发。亚美尼亚军区早已沿高加索南下至基利家的弧形地带设立，但还有一条迁移路径：原先的王室家族被迁往罗马统治下的卡帕多基亚。一部编年史大幅简化了事情的来龙去脉，直接把亚美尼亚人的迁徙归因于王室家族的迁置。
这一迁置关系到罗曼尼亚如何治理少数族群，一些学者对它的描述却容易引起误解。对瓦斯普拉坎、阿尼与卡尔斯王室的迁置，有一种“最大限度”的解释，认为他们在卡帕多基亚获封幅员辽阔、可以世袭、享有相当自治权的亚美尼亚“公国”，靠从亚美尼亚带来的封建军队进行统治。他们甚至推行自己的“外交政策”，有时针对帝国本身。

en: The maximalist position is untenable and is not supported by the sources, whether Roman or Armenian. Such a grant would be a radical departure from prior imperial policy, an unprecedented and unnecessary surrender of sovereignty made, puzzlingly, from a position of strength, for the first of these grants was made by Basileios II around 1020. He was not one to devolve power, especially after having fought so many wars to consolidate it into his hands. The sources for the period, many of them written by contemporaries, are unaware of the existence of such huge Armenian statelets in the heart of Roman Asia Minor. The actual arrangement was far more prosaic. The facts support a minimalist interpretation according to which the royals were given land, titles, and minor commands of a more limited geographical scope, not new personal principalities in exchange for their old ones.
Let us look at the evidence.
zh: 这种最大限度的解释站不住脚，无论罗马还是亚美尼亚史料都无法支持它。这类封授在既有的帝国政策中没有先例，等于毫无必要地放弃主权。更令人费解的是，最早的一次封授出自约1020年正占据强势地位的瓦西里二世。他打了那么多仗才把权力收归己手，岂肯再把它下放？记述这一时期的史料有不少出自同时代人之手，却没有一部提到在罗马小亚细亚腹地存在这么大的亚美尼亚小国。实际安排平常得多。事实支持一种最限缩的解释：王室成员获授土地、头衔和管辖范围较小的指挥职，并没有拿旧公国换得新的私人公国。
且来看证据。

en: The sources say that in exchange for Vaspurakan, its ruler was given the title of

and placed in command of the cities of Sebasteia, Larissa, and Abara. He was also given much landed property, to which he moved with a large following. His family and retinue are thereafter associated with Sebasteia.
There is uncertainty about whether this grant was received by Senekʿerim or his son Davitʿ, who was also known as Senekʿerim.

If it was the former, then an allowance was made for the “hereditary” transmission of the grant from father to son in 1027, when the father died—the only instance of such transmission that the entire settlement of all the royals entailed. This would not have been difficult for Basileios to arrange, as he had experimented with heredity in his imperial arrangements before.

If Davitʿ was the original recipient, as seems more likely, then we face no such issue: he was simply accommodated within the existing imperial administration. Now, the twelfth-century Armenian historian Matthew of Edessa claims that two years later Basileios gave Kaisareia, Tzamandos, and Gabadonia to Davitʿ as a reward for his murder of the rebel Nikephoros Phokas, in 1022. This information about the additional grant appears only in Matthew and must be treated with caution, in fact with skepticism. Matthew is unreliable, often purveying fiction as history (see below). It is possible that Basileios gave Davitʿ
Kaisareia or

Tzamandos, but it is virtually impossible that he gave that city and that district to him. Kaisareia (in Charsianon theme) was a central node in the empire’s military organization and is never associated in Byzantine sources with Davitʿ.
zh: 史料说，作为交出瓦斯普拉坎的补偿，其统治者被授予
（patrikios）头衔，并受命指挥塞巴斯泰亚、拉里萨与阿巴拉诸城。他还获授大量地产，携大批追随者迁往那里。此后他的家族与扈从便与塞巴斯泰亚相关联。
这份封授究竟由塞内克里姆还是由同样以塞内克里姆之名见称的儿子达维特领受，尚无定论。
若是前者，那么1027年父亲去世时，封授当时获准由父传子。这便是安置各家王室时唯一一桩“世袭”。这样的做法对瓦西里并不难，他先前已在帝国的制度安排中试过世袭。
若达维特是最初领受者（这似乎更可能），那么这桩世袭便无从谈起。他只是被纳入既有的帝国行政体系。十二世纪亚美尼亚史家埃德萨的马太声称，两年后瓦西里把凯撒利亚、扎曼多斯与加巴多尼亚赐给达维特，作为对他1022年谋杀叛乱者尼基弗鲁斯·福卡斯的奖赏。这桩追加封授只见于马太笔下，须谨慎对待，甚至有理由怀疑。马太常把虚构故事当作历史，记述并不可靠（见下文）。瓦西里可能给了达维特凯撒利亚
的土地或扎曼多斯
的土地，但几乎不可能把那座城市本身和那个区本身给他。凯撒利亚（在哈尔西亚农军区）是帝国军事组织的一个中心节点，在拜占庭史料中从未与达维特相关联。

en: Gagik II of Ani had surrendered Ani to the empire reluctantly, after it had been pledged by his uncle. In around 1045 Konstantinos IX Monomachos gave him the title of
and lands in Cappadocia, Charsianon, and Lykandos—not command of the themes, just lands
them. Matthew of Edessa names the lands as Kalon-Peghat and Pizu.

Two contemporary Roman sources say that Gagik “thereafter lived a peaceful and untroubled life” (Skylitzes), and “spent the rest of his charmed life in luxury and enjoyment on account of the properties and superlative titles that he was given” (Attaleiates).

It is important to quote these passages because they refute the hagiographic-heroic account of Gagik’s later career in Matthew of Edessa. Matthew has the deposed king deliver long sermons on Armenian Christianity to the imperial court; order his Armenian soldiers to rape Roman women by Kaisareia as he was passing through; then murder the bishop of Kaisareia who was prejudiced against Armenians; and plot to have his throne restored by the Seljuks—all in the time before both Attaleiates and Skylitzes were writing. For Matthew, Gagik symbolized Armenian strength and uncompromising faith.
zh: 阿尼的加吉克二世在叔父已答应将阿尼交给帝国的情况下，勉强答应交出这座城。约1045年，君士坦丁九世·莫诺马霍斯授予他
（magistros）头衔，以及卡帕多基亚、哈尔西亚农与利坎多斯的土地——不是军区的指挥权，只是军区
的土地。埃德萨的马太把这些土地称为卡隆佩加特与皮祖。
两部同时代罗马史料说，加吉克“此后过了平静无忧的生活”（斯基利齐斯），并“因获授的财产与无上头衔，得以锦衣玉食，安享余生”（阿塔雷阿特斯）。
引用这些段落很重要，因为它们驳斥了埃德萨的马太对加吉克后期生涯的圣徒传式的英雄叙事。在马太笔下，这位失位的国王向帝国宫廷发表关于亚美尼亚基督教的长篇布道；命他的亚美尼亚士兵在途经凯撒利亚时强奸罗马妇女；随后谋杀对亚美尼亚人怀有偏见的凯撒利亚主教；并密谋让塞尔柱人帮他复辟王位——这些事据称全都发生在阿塔雷阿特斯和斯基利齐斯写作之前。对马太而言，加吉克象征着亚美尼亚的力量与不妥协的信仰。

en: Matthew also believed that Davitʿ (formerly of Vaspurakan) died in the mid-1030s and passed the command of Sebasteia to his brother Atom, which would make this the second hereditary transfer in the settlement of the royals of Vaspurakan.

But he was mistaken. Aristakes, a more reliable historian who was writing closer to the events, says that, “by order of the emperor Konstantinos IX, Gagik married Davitʿs daughter and ruled that sector [i.e., Sebasteia], since when Davitʿ died he had left no other heir.”
There was, then, no hereditary transfer, only an imperial reassignment.
Sebasteia passed to Gagik, which explains why he is often present there in Matthew’s subsequent narrative, although he did not know about the reassignment.
In the 1070s, after the battle of Mantzikert, Gagik was given the position of
of Charsianon, though it is unknown what (if any) responsibilities it entailed at that point.

By contrast, Davitʿs brothers Atom and Abusahl are not attested with titles or offices, despite their prominence in Matthew’s narrative. Finally, the last Armenian king to cede his realm to the empire was Gagik of Kars, around 1064. Matthew claims that the emperor (Konstantinos X Doukas) gave him Tzamandos (in Lykandos) in which to settle with his noblemen (that theme had been settled by Armenians from its tenth-century beginnings).
zh: 马太还以为，原先统治瓦斯普拉坎的达维特死于1030年代中期，并把塞巴斯泰亚的指挥权传给其兄弟阿托姆，这将使此事成为瓦斯普拉坎王室安置中的第二次世袭传承。
但他错了。阿里斯塔克斯是一位更可靠、写作时间更接近事件的史家，他说，“奉皇帝君士坦丁九世之命，加吉克娶了达维特的女儿并统治那个区［即塞巴斯泰亚］，因为达维特去世时没有留下其他继承人”。
因此，这是皇帝重新任命的人选，并非世袭。
塞巴斯泰亚改由阿尼的加吉克管辖，这解释了为何在马太随后的叙事中他常出现在那里，尽管马太不知道这一任命。
1070年代，曼齐克特战役之后，加吉克被授予哈尔西亚农
（megas doux）之职，尽管那时它究竟附带何种（若有）职责不得而知。
相比之下，达维特的兄弟阿托姆与阿布萨赫尔虽在马太叙事中显赫，却未见有头衔或官职记载。最后，把王国割让给帝国的末代亚美尼亚国王是卡尔斯的加吉克，时间约为1064年。马太声称皇帝（君士坦丁十世·杜卡斯）把扎曼多斯（在利坎多斯）赐给他，让他与贵族们定居其中（该军区自十世纪创立之初就有亚美尼亚人定居）。

en: In sum, there is no proof for quasi-autonomous Armenian principalities established within Roman territory. The royals were given lands on which to settle and one command, that of Sebasteia, which was reallocated to Gagik of Ani when Davitʿ died; Gagik may later have been given a command in Charsianon. The question then arises not only about how Romans ruled Armenians, but how former Armenian kings ruled Romans in the theme of Sebasteia. Unfortunately, we have no evidence about that.
zh: 总之，没有证据表明罗马领土内建立了准自治的亚美尼亚公国。王室成员获授土地定居，拿到的指挥权也仅有塞巴斯泰亚一处。达维特去世后，这一职位由阿尼的加吉克接任。加吉克后来可能又在哈尔西亚农获任指挥职。于是问题不仅在于罗马人如何统治亚美尼亚人，还在于前亚美尼亚国王如何在塞巴斯泰亚军区统治罗马人。遗憾的是，我们对此没有证据。

en: Be that as it may, these resettlements did not result in surrogate Armenian statehood, nor were they intended to do so. Still, they played a crucial historical role, one that was enabled by the emperors. The deposed royal families supported the Armenian Church in the empire, hosting the
on their new lands, building churches and monasteries, and forming a nucleus that drew more Armenians from the homeland, as it became increasingly unsafe.

The royals did not have private or royal armies, but they did have retinues and wealth, with which they attracted more clients. In these ways, they facilitated the Armenian drift westward and southward. What is important for our purposes is that the emperors let them do this. The idea that the royals turned violent against Romanía is due entirely to the nationalist and theological polemics of Matthew of Edessa, who treats the deposed royals as heroic champions against the wicked Byzantines. But the stories that he tells about this are unbelievable, for instance that Romanos IV Diogenes sacked the city of Sebasteia on his way to Mantzikert out of sheer hatred of the Armenian faith.

Despite Matthew’s polemics and his hints of persecutions that were intended but did not actually happen, Romanía tolerantly accommodated its anti-Chalcedonian Armenians. The latter, especially the former royals, resisted the allure of Constantinople by refusing to convert, and their families accordingly did not advance high in imperial service. Nina Garsoïan concludes that “the overwhelming mass of the Armenian inhabitants of the empire, isolated by language more than by ethnic background, by religion . . . and at last by the mythology surrounding their lost king [Gagik], remained alien and alienated—incorporated but not assimilated.”
zh: 总之，迁置王室无意重建亚美尼亚国家，也没有产生这种结果。然而，皇帝促成的这些安排在历史上仍起了关键作用。被废黜的王室家族在帝国境内支持亚美尼亚教会，在其新土地上接待
（katholikoi），修建教堂与修道院，并形成一个核心，随着故土日益不安全，吸引更多亚美尼亚人前来。
王室成员没有私人或王室军队，但他们确有扈从与财富，用以招揽更多依附者，由此推动亚美尼亚人向西、向南迁徙。这里值得注意的是，这一切都得到皇帝的默许。王室成员据称曾对罗曼尼亚动武，这个说法完全来自埃德萨的马太的民族主义与神学论战，他把被废黜的王室当作对抗邪恶拜占庭人的英雄斗士。但他讲述的这类故事不可信，例如罗曼努斯四世·第欧根尼在前往曼齐克特途中纯粹出于对亚美尼亚信仰的仇恨而洗劫塞巴斯泰亚城。
尽管马太有论战，并暗示有些迫害本打算实施却并未实际发生，罗曼尼亚仍宽容地容纳了其反卡尔西顿派亚美尼亚人。后者，尤其前王室成员，通过拒绝改宗而抵制君士坦丁堡的诱惑，他们的家族也因此未在帝国仕途中高升。尼娜·加尔索扬总结说：“帝国境内绝大多数亚美尼亚居民，由于语言上的隔阂（其影响超过族群出身）、宗教……最后还有围绕失位国王［加吉克］的传说，仍处在孤立和疏离之中。他们虽被纳入帝国，却未被同化。”

en: The attitudes toward the empire of its new Armenian subjects reflected this sense of incorporation without assimilation. Basileios II had sent a fragment of the True Cross to a monastery in Vaspurakan (outside his dominions), which earned him a panegyric by the Armenian poet Grigor of Narek in the 990s. Here doctrinal differences were set aside. But the works produced by Armenians in the eleventh century keep their distance and do not identify with the empire. The historian Step’anos was born around the time that his homeland Taron was voluntarily annexed—an event that he mentions—and he used at least one Greek source in writing about recent events (he finished writing in 1003 or 1004). But he seems to have worked in Ani, outside the empire. He does not depict the empire as an evil foreign oppressor, but he did regard it as a threat to Armenian identity and its Church; he does not engage in polemics against the Romans, only their theology.

Aristakes of Lastivert, a historian of the eleventh century, was from a town near the Roman command center of Theodosioupolis (annexed in 1000). He also used a Greek source and is not overtly hostile to the Romans as such, though he bewails and castigates their failure to defend the east from the Turks. Thus, like the Jews of southern Italy and the Bulgarians, Armenians under Roman rule continued to produce narratives that affirmed their ethnic or national distinction from the imperial core.
zh: 新臣民对帝国的态度，就反映出亚美尼亚人被纳入却未同化的处境。瓦西里二世曾把真十字架的一块碎片送到瓦斯普拉坎的一所修道院（在他领土之外），这为他在990年代赢得亚美尼亚诗人纳雷克的格里戈尔的一篇颂词。这里教义分歧被搁置。但十一世纪亚美尼亚人创作的作品保持距离，不认同帝国。史家斯捷潘诺斯出生于故乡塔隆自愿并入帝国前后——他提到了这一事件——他在叙述近事时至少用了一部希腊史料（他于1003或1004年完成写作）。但他似乎在帝国之外的阿尼工作。他不把帝国描绘为邪恶的外国压迫者，但确实视之为对亚美尼亚认同及其教会的威胁；他不参与针对罗马人的论战，只针对他们的神学。
拉斯蒂韦特的阿里斯塔克斯是十一世纪的一位史家，来自狄奥多西乌波利斯（1000年被吞并）这个罗马指挥中心附近的一座城镇。他也用了一部希腊史料，对罗马人本身并不公然敌视，尽管他哀叹并谴责他们未能保卫东方免受突厥人侵害。因此，像南意大利的犹太人与保加尔人一样，罗马统治下的亚美尼亚人继续创作叙事，申明他们与帝国核心人口在族群或民族上的区别。

en: Georgians, Syrians, Melkites, Muslims, Jews
zh: 格鲁吉亚人、叙利亚人、麦尔基派、穆斯林、犹太人

en: Georgians (also known as Kartvelians, called Iberians by the Byzantines) had the same religion as the Romans, but we lack unambiguous evidence for assimilation on their part. The largest concentration of Georgians in the empire were in the part of Tao that was annexed in 1000, and Basileios II had prepared the ground before 1000 by bestowing imperial titles on local notables. But the impression left by the Georgians is that they maintained their ethnic separation even when they were actively involved in the affairs of the empire. They founded a separate monastery on Mt. Athos, called Iviron (“of the Iberians”), which had around three hundred monks in the eleventh century.

The imperial general Gregorios Pakourianos was of mixed Georgian-Armenian ancestry and culture but claimed to belong to “the most glorious race of the Georgians.” He had a distinguished career in Roman service in the eleventh century and died in battle against the Pechenegs. In the charter for the monastery that he founded in Bulgaria (Bačkovo), he notes that many of his relations had shed their blood fighting for the Roman empire and that he too was proud of serving it, but at the same time he stipulated that the monastery was for Georgians only, and he specifically excluded Romans from it because they were too violent and greedy, a remarkable assertion of ethnic stereotypes and boundaries.
zh: 格鲁吉亚人（也称卡特维尔人，拜占庭人称伊比利亚人）与罗马人信仰同一宗教，但没有明确证据表明格鲁吉亚人受到同化。帝国内格鲁吉亚人最集中的地方是1000年被吞并的那部分陶，瓦西里二世在1000年前就通过授予当地显贵帝国头衔做了铺垫。但格鲁吉亚人留下的印象是，即便积极参与帝国事务，他们仍维持自身的族群界限。他们在阿索斯山创立了一所独立修道院，称伊维龙（“伊比利亚人的”），十一世纪约有三百修士。

帝国将领格里戈里奥斯·帕库里亚诺斯有格鲁吉亚—亚美尼亚混合血统与文化，却自称属于“最荣耀的格鲁吉亚族裔”。十一世纪，他在罗马帝国任将领，战功显著，最终在与佩切涅格人的战斗中阵亡。在他于保加利亚创立的修道院（巴奇科沃）的建院章程中，他提到许多亲属曾为罗马帝国流血作战，他自己也以服务帝国为荣，但同时规定该修道院仅限格鲁吉亚人，并特别把罗马人排除在外，因为他们太暴戾贪婪——这番话将针对他人的族群成见和本群体的界限说得格外直白。

en: In a compilation of decisions made by the early eleventh-century judge Eustathios Romaios, we find a case of an “ethnic” man of Georgian origin who held a high court title but had not followed “the laws of the Romans” in drawing up his will. Instead, he had followed his national custom, and the judge emended the will in accordance with Roman law in order to process the dispute.
In both cases (of founding monasteries and drawing up wills) it was the Georgians who maintained their own separation, not the imperial authorities who enforced it.
zh: 在十一世纪早期法官欧斯塔提奥斯·罗马约斯的判决汇编中，我们看到一个案例：一名格鲁吉亚出身的“异族”男子持有高级宫廷头衔，却在立遗嘱时未遵循“罗马人的法律”。相反，他遵循了自己的民族习俗，法官为处理纠纷便依罗马法修订了遗嘱。
在设立修道院和立遗嘱这两件事上，格鲁吉亚人都主动维持自己的界限，并非帝国当局强制划分。

en: As the empire expanded in the southeast, it incorporated members of the Syrian Orthodox faith (also known as Jacobites), who also did not recognize the Council of Chalcedon and were therefore regarded by the Byzantine Church effectively as heretical; by this point, the Syrian Orthodox were functionally an ethnicity too, distinguished by language, ecclesiastical organization, and a shared history.

Initially, the empire not only incorporated them, it actively encouraged them to leave Muslim-controlled lands and resettle on imperial territory. Nikephoros II Phokas (963–969) invited their patriarch Yuhannan VII Sarigta to relocate to Melitene, under assurance of toleration. The offer was accepted, but that same emperor later hauled the patriarch and his bishops to Constantinople, where they were forced to debate doctrinal issues. Toleration was restored by the more pragmatic Ioannes I Tzimiskes (969–976), and soon the Jacobites expanded their presence and built monasteries in the Roman-ruled east, especially around Melitene and Antioch, with financial assistance provided by court officials. The immigration of Jacobites and Armenians presumably filled the demographic and economic gap left by the Muslims who were expelled in the course of the Roman conquest (see below). The period of toleration of the Jacobites lasted sixty years, whereupon persecution of their ecclesiastical leadership was initiated again by Romanos III Argyros in 1029 and, after another hiatus, Konstantinos X Doukas in the 1060s, with more arrests, forced “debates,” and exiles. Konstantinos X allegedly intended to expel all non-Chalcedonians from Melitene.
zh: 随着帝国向东南扩张，叙利亚正教（又称雅各派）的信众被纳入帝国。他们同样不承认卡尔西顿公会议，因而被拜占庭教会视同异端。此时，叙利亚正教徒实际上也已构成一个族群，有独具特色的语言、教会组织和一段共同的历史。

起初，帝国不仅并入他们，还积极鼓励他们离开穆斯林控制的土地，迁居到帝国境内。尼基弗鲁斯二世·福卡斯（963—969年在位）邀请他们的牧首尤哈南七世·萨里格塔迁往梅利泰内，并保证予以宽容。邀请被接受了，但同一位皇帝后来却把牧首及其主教们押往君士坦丁堡，强迫他们就教义问题展开辩论。较为务实的约安尼斯一世·齐米斯凯斯（969—976年在位）恢复了宽容，不久雅各派便在罗马统治下的东方各地壮大，兴建修道院，尤其是在梅利泰内和安条克一带，并得到宫廷官员的财政资助。雅各派与亚美尼亚人的迁入，想必填补了罗马征服过程中被驱逐的穆斯林所留下的人口与经济空缺（见下文）。对雅各派的宽容时期持续了六十年，此后罗曼努斯三世·阿尔吉罗斯于1029年再度发起对其教会领导层的迫害，又经一段间歇后，君士坦丁十世·杜卡斯在1060年代继续迫害，伴随着更多的逮捕、强迫“辩论”和流放。据称君士坦丁十世打算把所有非卡尔西顿派逐出梅利泰内。

en: Clearly, a politics of difference marked the empire’s treatment of Jacobites, especially their priesthood, more so, it seems, than its treatment of the equally non-Chalcedonian Armenians. As we saw, some of the latter were appointed to high Roman offices in the east, but I know of no Jacobites similarly promoted between the bouts of ecclesiastical persecution.

A synod convened in 1030 in Constantinople to condemn the Jacobites reminded the emperors that the laws of the Christian Roman empire forbade such heretics from holding court titles as well as civic and military positions.

And yet Armenian non-Chalcedonians were being appointed to high offices. Moreover, it appears that the ancient laws against heretics were not always enforced on the Jacobites either. The Byzantine Orthodox bishop of Melitene Ioannes complained to the patriarch and Synod of Constantinople about this, and they drafted a resolution protesting the nonenforcement of the relevant laws. Apparently, Orthodox families were marrying their daughters to the Jacobites; the latter were being allowed to draft legal wills naming other heretics as their heirs; and judges were admitting testimony given by Jacobites against the Orthodox, all of which was prohibited by law.
It seems that a politics of difference was not being vigorously enforced in Melitene, and the two religious communities were being treated as legally interchangeable.
zh: 显然，帝国对雅各派实行区别对待，尤其是对其神职人员。比起同属非卡尔西顿派的亚美尼亚人，雅各派所受的差别待遇看来更明显。如前所见，后者有人在帝国东部获任要职，但在两轮教会迫害之间，我不知道有哪个雅各派获得类似的擢升。
1030年在君士坦丁堡召开的一次主教会议谴责雅各派，并提醒诸位皇帝：基督教罗马帝国的法律禁止此类异端持有宫廷头衔以及民政与军事职位。
然而，非卡尔西顿派的亚美尼亚人却仍有人获任要职。此外，针对异端的古代法律似乎也并不总是对雅各派严格执行。梅利泰内的拜占庭正教主教约安尼斯就此事向君士坦丁堡牧首及主教会议投诉，他们起草了一份决议，抗议相关法律未获执行。显然，正教家庭把女儿嫁给雅各派；后者获准订立有法律效力的遗嘱，指定其他异端为继承人；法官也采纳雅各派针对正教徒所作的证词——而这一切都是法律所禁止的。
看来在梅利泰内，当局并未严格实行区别对待，两个宗教群体在实际适用法律时受到同等对待。

en: We need more research on the selective enforcement of these laws by region, community, and date. Among the nonreligious factors relevant to the exclusion of the Syrians from high office was their lack of prior experience in running states and armies, whether their own or those of a host empire, whereas many Armenians had such experience.
zh: 我们需要更多研究，考察这些法律按地区、共同体和年代而选择性执行的情况。在导致叙利亚人被排除于高级官职之外的非宗教因素中，有一条是他们此前缺乏管理国家、统率军队的经验，无论是管理自身的国家和军队，还是为接纳他们的帝国效力。而许多亚美尼亚人则具备这种经验。

en: The multiethnic demography of the major cities in the Roman east is illustrated by a history of the Coptic patriarchs of Alexandria (an Arabic text), which records that in 1072 Edessa had 20,000 Syrians, 8,000 Armenians, 6,000 Romans, and 1,000 Latins (including probably Frankish mercenaries).
Even if these figures are accurate, they do not necessarily reflect the city’s demography in the more settled decades before the Turkish invasions that were taking place at that time.
zh: 一部阿拉伯语的亚历山大里亚科普特牧首史，列出了一个例子，说明罗马帝国东部大城市的多族群人口构成。该书记载，1072年埃德萨有20,000名叙利亚人、8,000名亚美尼亚人、6,000名罗马人和1,000名拉丁人（可能包括法兰克雇佣兵）。
即使这些数字准确，那时突厥人正在入侵，据此也未必能推断入侵前相对安定的几十年间埃德萨的人口构成。

en: Imperial expansion also brought in a large population of Arabic-speaking Orthodox (also known as Melkites). They may have formed a majority of the population in Cilicia, especially after the expulsion of the Muslims, as well as in Antioch and its hinterland. Antioch became a forward base or second capital of the empire on the frontier. It was only to be expected that the empire would favor Melkites in the new territories. It relied on them to govern Antioch at the local level, preferring them over the Armenians and Jacobites. The Melkite Church consolidated its power there and sometimes harassed the Churches of its rivals, even when the latter were being tolerated by the imperial authorities elsewhere. The Melkite population of Antioch and Laodikeia was also boosted by refugees fleeing the chaotic regime of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim in Egypt in the mid-1010s; among them was the later historian Yahya of Antioch, a Melkite who wrote in Arabic.

His chronicle, one of the best works of history of its time, does not focus on his Church or its dispersed membership, though it does recount the events of the tenth and eleventh centuries from its perspective. But the fascinating and complex history of Antioch during the century of Roman rule has not yet been written in full, nor have studies yet been devoted to the treatment of Arabic-speaking Christians in Byzantium.
zh: 帝国扩张还将大量讲阿拉伯语的正教徒纳入治下（又称麦尔基派）。他们在基利家可能占人口多数，尤其是在穆斯林被驱逐之后。在安条克及其腹地，他们也可能占多数。安条克成为帝国在边境上的前进基地或第二都城。帝国在新领土上偏袒麦尔基派，是意料之中的事。在安条克的地方治理上，比起亚美尼亚人和雅各派，帝国更为倚重麦尔基派。麦尔基派教会在那里巩固了自己的权力，有时还骚扰其对手的教会，即便后者在别处正受到帝国当局的宽容。1010年代中期，有难民逃离埃及法蒂玛王朝哈里发哈基姆治下的乱局，来到安条克和劳迪基亚（Laodikeia），使当地麦尔基派人口增加；其中就有后来的历史学家、以阿拉伯语写作的麦尔基派信徒安条克的叶哈雅。
他的编年史是当时最出色的史著之一，虽以其教会的视角记述十、十一世纪的事件，却并不聚焦于该教会或其分散的信众。但安条克在罗马统治那一百年间引人入胜而复杂的历史，至今尚未被完整书写，也还没有研究专门探讨拜占庭境内说阿拉伯语基督徒的处境。

en: I have not found characterizations of Melkite Christians in Roman texts of this period from which we might gauge their perception of ethnic or cultural difference. The twelfth-century Armenian historian Matthew of Edessa says that the Melkites of Antioch (or some subgroup) “consider themselves Romans in faith but in essence should be regarded as Muslims because of the language they use and because of their deeds.” But he is a hostile witness, going on to call them “blasphemers of the Orthodox faith [he means his own anti-Chalcedonian faith] . . . resembling sick and feeble women who sit in the streets and babble with their tongues.”

The Romans would obviously have had a different view. The empire had in the past accepted Christians from the caliphate and resettled them, though before the ninth century most would have been Greek-speakers.
Some Arabic-speakers among them were promoted to high offices in the administration.

In our period, the empire did give court titles to Melkites. It is likely that an Arabic-speaking Christian, Kulayb, who was promoted to the highest position available locally, governor of Antioch, was a Melkite. However, such appointments were made under tense circumstances of conquest and civil war; thereafter that post was held by career Roman officers.
zh: 在这一时期的罗马文本中，我没有找到对麦尔基派基督徒的刻画，可供判断罗马人当时如何看待这种族群或文化差异。十二世纪亚美尼亚历史学家埃德萨的马太说，安条克的麦尔基派（或其某个分支）“自以为信仰上是罗马人，可从他们说的语言和所作所为来看，本质上应当把他们视为穆斯林”但他是一个怀有敌意的见证者，接着又称他们为“正教信仰的亵渎者［他指的是他自己的反卡尔西顿派信仰］……好比坐在街边喋喋不休的病弱妇人”
罗马人显然会有不同的看法。帝国过去曾接纳来自哈里发国的基督徒并安置他们，不过在九世纪之前，他们大多说希腊语。
其中一些说阿拉伯语的人获任行政要职。
在我们讨论的时期，帝国确曾授予麦尔基派信徒宫廷头衔。一位说阿拉伯语的基督徒库莱布被擢升为当地可获得的最高职位——安条克总督，他很可能就是麦尔基派。不过，这类任命是在征服与内战的紧张局势下作出的；此后该职位便由职业罗马军官担任。

en: The leadership of the Melkite community, both lay and clerical, possibly retained a knowledge of Greek, which had remained an important language in the Christian East long after the Arab conquests. This means that they would have been able to interface seamlessly with the Roman administration and even pass in Roman society. The epitaph of one Basileios, who died in Antioch in 999, was written in both Greek and Arabic.
More light on this question will likely be brought by the publication of bilingual Arabic-Greek seals from the collection at Dumbarton Oaks, especially those that record offices and titles.
zh: 麦尔基派中掌事的平信徒和教士可能仍通晓希腊语。阿拉伯征服后很长一段时间，希腊语在东方基督徒中仍是一种重要语言。这样一来，他们便可顺畅地同罗马行政当局打交道，甚至能在罗马社会中被视作罗马人。999年卒于安条克的一位瓦西里的墓志铭，用希腊语和阿拉伯语两种文字写成。
敦巴顿橡树园藏品中阿拉伯语和希腊语双语印章的公布，尤其是那些记录官职和头衔的印章，很可能会为这一问题带来更多线索。

en: Another Melkite, Petros Libellisios, was appointed governor of Antioch around 1068. He is described as follows by the historian Michael Attaleiates: “He was Assyrian by race, born in Antioch, and he had been superbly educated in both Roman and Saracen wisdom and letters.”

In other words, he was bilingual, perhaps bicultural, and educated in a way that an elite Roman could respect. It would be curious to know how Melkites who spoke no Greek were perceived by Romans, say, for example, by Constantinopolitans, for Melkites were not Arabic-speaking Romans: they had their own, separate identity.

Still, imperial policy seems not to have enforced or even formally recognized ethnic, linguistic, or cultural differences between these two Orthodox groups, however Greek- and Arabic-speakers perceived each other.
zh: 另一位麦尔基派彼得罗斯·利贝利西奥斯约在1068年被任命为安条克总督。历史学家米海尔·阿塔雷阿特斯如此描述他：“他按族属是亚述人，生于安条克，在罗马与萨拉森的智慧与学问两方面都受过极好的教育。”
换言之，他通晓两种语言，或许也熟悉两种文化，所受的教育足以赢得罗马精英的敬重。令人好奇的是，那些不说希腊语的麦尔基派在罗马人眼中——比方说在君士坦丁堡人眼中——是何形象，因为麦尔基派并不是说阿拉伯语的罗马人：他们拥有自己独立的身份认同。
尽管如此，无论希腊语者和阿拉伯语者如何看待彼此，帝国似乎并未依两支正教群体在族群、语言或文化上的差异施行区别对待，甚至并未在制度上承认这些差异。

en: Muslims bore the brunt of the empire’s military expansion in the east, which targeted a number of frontier emirates from Cilicia, up through Melitene, to those nestled more deeply in the southern Caucasus.

The Roman expansion was perceived by Muslims abroad as an unmitigated disaster, eliciting calls for jihad and, when those failed, lamentations and fiery sermons. It was inevitable that the empire would now have Muslim subjects, but they were perhaps not as many as one might conclude from looking at a map. The Roman campaigns of conquest against the emirates were brutal, targeting the civilian population, destroying agriculture, and enslaving those who were caught in the countryside. Many of those captives were brought back to the core territories and dispersed as slaves. Nikephoros II Phokas in particular tended to expel Muslims from the cities that he captured during the fifteen years when he was in command of the army (955–969), or to demand that they convert. This caused depopulation. The sources, both Roman and Arab, contain many references to columns of refugees departing for more distant Muslim lands, sometimes under military escort. In order to keep or reclaim their homes, some Muslims converted, presumably to the Melkite Church, sometimes after they had been initially deported. With regard to Muslims, then, Romanía practiced an imperial “politics of difference” at its most extreme, at least initially.
zh: 穆斯林首当其冲地承受了帝国在东方的军事扩张，其矛头指向一系列边境埃米尔国，从基利家北上经梅利泰内，直至更深入高加索南部的那些埃米尔国。

罗马人的扩张被境外穆斯林视为一场彻头彻尾的灾难，激起了发动吉哈德（圣战）的呼吁，呼吁失败后又引出哀叹与激昂的布道。帝国如今拥有穆斯林臣民是不可避免的，但他们的人数或许不像看地图所能推断的那样多。罗马人对埃米尔国的征服战役十分残酷，以平民为目标，摧毁农业，并将他们在乡间掳获的人贬为奴隶。许多俘虏被带回帝国腹地，分送各处为奴。尼基弗鲁斯二世·福卡斯尤其倾向于把穆斯林逐出他统率军队的十五个年头（955—969）中所夺取的城市，或要求他们改宗。这造成了人口锐减。罗马与阿拉伯史料都大量提到难民队伍离境前往更遥远的穆斯林土地，有时还有军队押送。为了保住或夺回家园，一些穆斯林改宗了，想必是皈依麦尔基派，其中一些人在被逐之后才改宗。因此，就穆斯林而言，罗曼尼亚践行了一种最极端的帝国“差异政治”，至少在起初如此。

en: After reducing the Muslim presence in the conquered territories, the state brought in Roman, Armenian, and Jacobite settlers (the last especially to the region of Melitene). It is possible also that the Christian population had been in the majority in Cilicia before the conquest, even if the emirates were governed by Muslims.
But after the conquests, Muslims were allowed to remain in some of the territories controlled by the

of Antioch. Unfortunately, we have no systematic study of how the empire governed them. It is likely that they largely governed themselves and interfaced with imperial authorities only at the highest local level. In some places, they were governed internally by their own judges, laws, and customs, while paying tribute to the empire.

A Nestorian Christian physician from Baghdad, Ibn Butlan, wrote in the mid-eleventh century that the main mosque of Laodikeia (on the Syrian coast) had been turned into a church but local Muslims prayed at another mosque and had their own judge
at a village between Antioch and Aleppo there were four Byzantine Orthodox (or Melkite) churches and one mosque.
zh: 征服地区的穆斯林人口减少之后，当局安排罗马人、亚美尼亚人和雅各派信徒迁入（后者尤其迁往梅利泰内地区）。也有可能，在征服之前基利家的基督徒人口本就占多数，即便那些埃米尔国由穆斯林统治。
但征服之后，穆斯林获准留在安条克
（doukaton）控制的部分领土上。遗憾的是，我们没有关于帝国如何治理他们的系统研究。他们很可能主要自行管理，只有地方最高一级的领袖才与帝国当局打交道。有些地方的穆斯林沿用自己的法律和习俗，由自己的法官裁断纠纷，同时向帝国纳贡。
一位来自巴格达的聂斯脱利派基督徒医师伊本·布特兰在十一世纪中叶写道，劳迪基亚（在叙利亚沿海）的主清真寺已被改为教堂，但当地穆斯林在另一座清真寺祈祷，并有自己的法官
（qadi）；在安条克与阿勒颇之间的一个村庄，有四座拜占庭正教（即麦尔基派）教堂和一座清真寺。

en: The empire did not want or seek out Muslim subjects, but it acquired and tolerated some because it needed their lands and cities for strategic reasons, for example in coastal Syria. As far as I know, Roman sources do not refer to them at all after the period of the conquests, or make ethnic distinctions among them (e.g., Arabs, Turks, Daylami, etc.). The Romans so hated their religion that this overrode finer internal distinctions. Progress in understanding the standing of these Muslim minorities in the Christian empire will likely come from further research in eastern sources.
zh: 帝国并不想要、也不刻意寻求穆斯林臣民，但出于战略需要吞并了他们的一些城市和土地（如叙利亚沿海），也就接纳了一些穆斯林臣民，容许他们留下。据我所知，罗马史料在征服时期之后完全不再提及他们，也不在他们内部作族群区分（如阿拉伯人、突厥人、代拉米人等）。罗马人对伊斯兰教的敌意如此之深，以致盖过了穆斯林内部更细微的差别。若想进一步弄清这些穆斯林少数群体在基督教帝国中的地位，恐怕还得从东方史料入手。

en: Imperial expansion in the east also brought more Jewish communities into the empire. Also, the intolerant climate of Fatimid Egypt led many Jews (as well as Melkites) to migrate to Romanía, which was flourishing economically. The empire was now crisscrossed by denser Jewish networks that extended throughout the eastern Mediterranean and into Muslim-ruled lands. Overall, these Jewish communities appear to have flourished too. The Nestorian bishop Elias of Nisibis (d. 1046) wrote that the Romans “tolerate a large population of Jews in their realm. . . . They afford them protection, allow them openly to adhere to their religion, and to build their synagogues. . . . The Jew in their lands may say ‘I am a Jew.’ No one brings it up to him, restrains him, or puts any difficulties in his way.” Yet in another part of the same treatise Elias says the Jews “endure humiliation and hatred.”
zh: 帝国在东方的扩张还把更多犹太共同体纳入帝国。此外，埃及法蒂玛王朝治下的宗教不宽容氛围促使许多犹太人（以及麦尔基派）迁往经济繁荣的罗曼尼亚。犹太社群的联系由此更加紧密，形成了贯穿帝国和东地中海、远及穆斯林治下的网络。总体而言，这些社群似乎也相当兴旺。聂斯脱利派主教尼西比斯的埃利亚斯（卒于1046年）写道，罗马人“在其境内宽容大量犹太人口……他们给予保护，允许他们公开信奉自己的宗教、兴建犹太会堂……在他们土地上的犹太人可以说‘我是犹太人’。没有人拿这事指责他、限制他，或给他设置任何障碍。”然而在同一篇论著的另一处，埃利亚斯又说犹太人“忍受屈辱与仇恨”。

en: The letters of the Cairo Genizah illustrate both aspects, but primarily the brighter one. In around 1090, a blind scholar, formerly from Egypt but now resident in Thessalonike, talks about the economic motives and concern for his safety that led him to migrate to the empire. Now, he says, “my situation is very good.”

In 1137, a Jew in Seleukeia (Isauria) claimed that he was prospering and that his contact would not regret joining him “here in the Land of the Romans. . . . This is a place which has everything in the world, just like the Fayyum.” The letter writer had married a local girl and referred to the Roman armies as “our commanders.” He was doing well and identified with Romanía.

By contrast, a letter from around 1096, obsessed with Messianic signs, says that in Thessalonike the Christians have always hated the Jews most intensely, but it also appears from this letter that the authorities were not being aggressive toward the Jewish community.
zh: 开罗藏经库（Cairo Genizah）的书信反映了这两方面的处境，更多呈现的是较好的一面。约1090年，一位从埃及迁居塞萨洛尼基的失明学者说，他来帝国是为谋生，也为自身安全考虑。他说，如今“我的境况非常好”。
1137年，塞琉基亚（伊苏里亚）的一位犹太人说自己过得很好，收信人来“这罗马人的土地上”与他相聚也不会后悔。“……此地什么都有，就像法尤姆一样。”写信者娶了一位当地姑娘，并用“我们的指挥官”指称罗马军队。他境况优裕，且认同罗曼尼亚。
相比之下，一封约写于1096年的信满篇谈的是弥赛亚降临的征兆，其中说，在塞萨洛尼基基督徒向来最强烈地憎恨犹太人，但从这封信也可看出，当局对犹太社群并未采取敌对行动。

en: Constantinople and the Armies
zh: 君士坦丁堡与军队

en: A baseline profile for Constantinople and the armies in 930 ad was established in Chapter 6, so here we need only briefly note major developments that occurred since that time.
zh: 第6章已勾勒出公元930年君士坦丁堡和军队的基本情形，因此这里只需简要记述此后发生的主要变化。

en: There is no evidence that Constantinople had become significantly more multiethnic by 1064, though it probably grew in population and was home to numerous royal hostages and deposed royal families. By the mid-eleventh century there was a permanent Latin community, which we know largely because some Latin-rite churches became bones of contention in the lead-up to the schism of 1054.

At first, the community was probably Amalfitan. In 992, the Venetians were made a favored trading partner with the empire: the treaty imagines that many of their ships would come to Constantinople, but it does not yet envisage a permanent presence.

The Latin community altogether probably numbered no more than a few hundred. In 1043, as a Rus’ naval attack became immanent, the authorities arrested all the Rus’ merchants in the City and dispersed them to the provinces, which suggests, first, that they were not too many; second, that there were no full-time Rus’ residents in the City; and third, that the authorities kept track of their whereabouts, which is what we would expect on the basis of the empire’s past treaties.
zh: 没有证据表明到1064年君士坦丁堡已变得明显更加多族群，尽管它的人口可能有所增长，并且收留了许多王室人质和失位王族。到十一世纪中叶，那里有了一个常驻的拉丁共同体，我们之所以知道这一点，主要是因为几座奉行拉丁礼的教堂在1054年教会分裂前夕成了争执的焦点。
起初，这个社群最初可能由阿马尔菲人组成。992年，威尼斯人成为帝国青睐的贸易伙伴：条约设想他们的许多船只将来到君士坦丁堡，但并未预见他们会在那里定居。
拉丁共同体总共大概不超过几百人。1043年，当罗斯人的一次海上袭击迫在眉睫时，当局逮捕了都城所有的罗斯商人，把他们分散到各行省，这表明：第一，他们人数不太多；第二，都城没有长住的罗斯人；第三，当局掌握着他们的行踪，而这正是我们根据帝国过去的条约所能预期的。

en: Moreover, the capital was now home to an array of dethroned kings and royal families, hostages from many surrounding polities and nations, embassies, and honored foreigners, but these did not significantly change its demography. A later Syriac source claims that Konstantinos IX expelled all the Armenians, Arabs, and Jews who had come to the capital in the past thirty years, allegedly because they had incited the riot against him in 1044 (which is nonsense). No reliable conclusions can be drawn from this testimony, as the author ridiculously says that the expulsion affected a hundred thousand people.
But it was under Konstantinos IX that we first hear of Roma (i.e., Gypsies) in Romanía. The emperor hired them to clear out some wild animals infesting the suburban Philopation park.
zh: 此外，都城如今接纳了许多失位君主和王族，也聚集了周边诸政权和民族送来的人质、使节，以及享有尊荣的外国人，但这些并未显著改变其人口构成。一部较晚的叙利亚语史料声称，君士坦丁九世驱逐了过去三十年来到都城的所有亚美尼亚人、阿拉伯人和犹太人，据称是因为他们煽动了1044年反对他的暴乱（这纯属无稽之谈）。从这一证词得不出任何可靠结论，因为作者荒谬地说驱逐影响了十万人。
