但正是在君士坦丁九世治下，史料首次记载罗曼尼亚出现罗姆人（旧称“吉卜赛人”）。皇帝雇用他们清除郊外菲洛帕提翁园林中肆虐的一些野兽。

en: A Latin description of Constantinople, by the “Anonymous Tarragonensis” and written toward the end of the eleventh century, says that the City contained many different
Greeks, Armenians, Syrians, Lombards, English, Dacians (probably Vlachs), Amalfitans, Franks, Jews, and Turks (or “Turkopouloi”), but that the Greeks occupied the largest and best part of the City.

The text strongly implies that each of these groups was assigned to a specific region, which we know was the case with the Jews and the growing Latin communities of that time. The City had become more multiethnic, though no ratios can be extracted from this list. The English mentioned here were Anglo-Saxon refugees who fled to Romanía after the Norman conquest of their homeland; many of them joined the Varangian Guard, which is likely who the author means here.

The Franks were likely also the mercenaries whom Alexios I Komnenos hired. The Syrians and Armenians had moved to Constantinople in the aftermath of the empire’s great expansion eastward or were pushed there by the Turkish expansion into Asia Minor, along with many Romans from Asia Minor.
zh: 一部由“塔拉戈纳匿名作者”（Anonymous Tarragonensis）撰写、成于十一世纪末的拉丁语君士坦丁堡描述说，都城有许多不同的
（族群）：希腊人、亚美尼亚人、叙利亚人、伦巴第人、英格兰人、达契亚人（可能是弗拉赫人）、阿马尔菲人、法兰克人、犹太人和突厥人（或称“突厥之子”Turkopouloi），但希腊人占据着都城最大、最好的部分。
从文意看，这些群体似乎各有划定的居住区。当时的犹太人和日益壮大的拉丁社群确是如此。都城已变得更加多族群，但凭这份名单无法推算各群体的人口比例。这里提到的英格兰人，是诺曼征服其家乡后逃往罗曼尼亚的盎格鲁-撒克逊难民；他们许多人加入了瓦良格卫队，作者此处很可能指的就是这些人。
法兰克人很可能也是阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁雇用的雇佣兵。叙利亚人和亚美尼亚人是在帝国大举向东扩张之后迁到君士坦丁堡的，也可能因突厥人向小亚细亚扩张而迁去，和他们一道迁去的还有许多小亚细亚的罗马人。

en: But before this period of dislocation, it is hard to accept the image of Constantinople as a cosmopolitan city; that is, beyond the boutique diversity of hostages, mercenaries, and merchants. The dominant attitude among the local authorities was likely the one expressed by Isaakios II Angelos when he said in a chrysobull of 1189 that, whereas it was not desirable to let the “nations” spread themselves in Constantinople, he was willing to except the Venetians, who loved Romanía so much that they were virtually like native Romans.
zh: 在这些人口流徙之前，很难把君士坦丁堡视为一座各国居民杂处的都会。带来几分异域色彩的，无非是少数人质、雇佣兵和商人。地方当局的主流态度，很可能就是伊萨克二世·安格洛斯在1189年一道金玺诏书中所表达的那种：他说，尽管不宜让各“民族”在君士坦丁堡广泛定居，但他愿意把威尼斯人作为例外，因为他们如此热爱罗曼尼亚，几乎就像土生土长的罗马人。

en: The Roman army definitely became more multiethnic in the later tenth and eleventh centuries, but not, as many historians believe, because it (allegedly) began to rely increasingly on foreign mercenaries. Actually, the numbers of such mercenaries were still low, consisting of groups of a few hundred here and there. Rather, the chief source of ethnolinguistic diversity in the army was the fact that the regular armies of the

of Bulgaria, Paradounabon, Vaspurakan, Iberia, and Edessa were surely recruited to some degree among the local populations, including Bulgarians, Georgians, and Armenians. In addition, a greater diversity of ethnic units is attested, raised among tributary or theoretically dependent people along the periphery, such as the Arvanites (Albanians), the Pechenegs in the lower Danube, and even Bedouin tribes from the Jazira. My sense is that they were hired or called up on an ad hoc basis and were not part of the standing forces. There was, however, one ethnic unit formed in this period that became a permanent institution, namely the self-consciously foreign Varangian Guard. Its very purpose was to be a corps that would have no Roman political interests and would therefore be exclusively loyal to its employer, the emperor. It was, after all, originally hired to fight against Roman armies in a civil war. Its “otherness” was therefore highlighted in many ways, and it is possible that its members were subject to separate legal status defined by the corps, comparable to other ethnic enclaves within the empire.
The Varangian Guard was an experiment in maintained but controlled ethnic difference.
zh: 罗马军队在十世纪后期和十一世纪确实变得更加多族群，但并非如许多历史学家所认为的那样，是因为它（据称）开始越来越依赖外国雇佣兵。实际上，这类雇佣兵的人数仍然很少，各处只有数百人一队。毋宁说，军中族群和语言日趋多样，主要因为保加利亚、帕拉多瑙纳冯（Paradounabon）、瓦斯普拉坎、伊比利亚和埃德萨各

（doukata）的正规军必然有一部分从当地居民中征募，包括保加尔人、格鲁吉亚人和亚美尼亚人。此外，史料还证实存在更多样的族群部队，它们沿周边地区从纳贡或理论上依附的民族中征召，例如阿尔瓦尼特人（阿尔巴尼亚人）、多瑙河下游的佩切涅格人，甚至来自贾兹拉（Jazira，美索不达米亚北部）的贝都因部落。在我看来，这些部队是临时雇用或征召的，并非常备军的一部分。然而，这一时期确实有一支族群部队成了常设制度，即自觉保持异族身份的瓦良格卫队。设立卫队正是为了拥有一支在罗马政争中没有自身利害、因而只效忠于雇主即皇帝的部队。毕竟，它最初被雇用，是为了在内战中对抗罗马军队。因此，它的“他者性”以多种方式被凸显，卫队成员可能遵循由该部队规定的单独法律身份，堪比帝国内部的其他族群飞地。
瓦良格卫队是帝国在可控条件下保留族群差异的一次尝试。

en: Law, Ethnicity, and Policy at the Apogee
zh: 极盛时期的法律、族群与政策

en: Some empires used formal instruments of law to enforce the unequal status of the conquerors and the conquered, to limit the latter’s access to the highest levels of power in the ruling hierarchy, and even to mark them off socially. Romanía was not such an empire. Within the lands governed by its formal institutions, its own legal system recognized the existence of only one law—Roman law—that applied to all its subjects. In a narrowly legal sense, the state “saw” only Roman citizens: “Those who live within the circumference of the Roman world, namely those who live under the authority of the Romans, even if they do not live in Rome itself, are still Roman citizens, on the basis of the decree issued by the emperor Antoninus” (i.e., the
After 212, Roman law eventually replaced the local laws of provincial cities, which, if they survived at all, become local customs operating at a sublegal level. The transition from an
full of
to a single-law Romanía can be traced in the sources.
zh: 有些帝国以正式的法律手段维持征服者与被征服者地位上的不平等，限制后者跻身统治集团最高层，甚至在社会上把他们区隔开来。罗曼尼亚不是这样的帝国。凡其正式制度所管辖之地，帝国法律体系只承认一部共同的法，即适用于全体臣民的罗马法。在狭义的法律意义上，国家只“看见”罗马公民：“身在罗马疆域之内的人，即受罗马人统治的人，即使并不居住在罗马城，按照安东尼努斯皇帝的敕令，也同样是罗马公民”（即212年的
，《安东尼努斯敕令》）。
212年之后，罗马法最终取代了行省城市的地方法律；这些地方法律即便幸存下来，也只作为地方习俗发挥作用，地位低于正式法律。从一个充满
（族群）的
（帝国）向单一法律的罗曼尼亚的转变，可以在史料中追踪到。

en: What is more difficult to discern is the legal treatment of foreign groups that entered the empire after 212, especially those that did so in large enough numbers to sustain a sense of their separate ethnicity, such as the Goths.
A legal scholion of the sixth century implies that the allied Gothic unit of the
was perceived as ethnically foreign and those who wished to join it had somehow to prove their ethnic eligibility.

And ethnic distinctions persisted within the empire’s core population, with the Bessians (Thracians) and Isaurians, for example, regarded sometimes as distinct groups. It is possible that Justinian appointed officers to “catch” Syrians and Egyptians and drive them away from the capital, an identification that would have been made on the basis of speech and other ethnic markers.
Roman legal homogeneity had not yet overridden all ethnic differences, though it was moving in that direction.
zh: 更难辨明的，是212年之后进入帝国的外国群体的法律待遇，尤其是那些人数多到足以维系其独立族群意识的群体，例如哥特人。
六世纪的一条法律评注暗示，哥特人组成的
（盟军部队）被视为异族，想加入的人必须设法证明自己的族属符合要求。
族群区分在帝国核心人口内部也持续存在，例如贝西人（色雷斯人）和伊苏里亚人有时就被视为不同的群体。查士丁尼可能曾任命官员去“抓捕”叙利亚人和埃及人，把他们驱离都城，官员应是凭说话方式和其他族群标志来辨认他们的。
罗马法制虽趋于统一，却还没有抹去所有族群差异。

en: We are in the dark when it comes to the legal status of foreign peoples conquered or annexed by the empire, such as the Tzanoi and Armenians placed under direct imperial rule by Justinian; also of lands in the core territories that were lost to foreign settlers and then reabsorbed along with their new ethnic populations, such as Bulgaria and the Sklabinias in Greece; and of foreign lands that had never been part of the core of the empire but were annexed in the later tenth and eleventh centuries, such as the various Caucasian principalities. Was Roman law introduced to these territories? Did the state treat their inhabitants as (notional or actual) Roman citizens, even if they did not assimilate culturally and ethnically, as so many clearly did not in the period that interests us here? They may have been viewed by Roman society as ethnically different, but did the state treat them as Roman citizens whenever they interacted with it formally?
zh: 我们无从得知帝国征服或吞并的外族享有什么法律地位，例如被查士丁尼置于帝国直接统治之下的茨阿诺伊人和亚美尼亚人。原属帝国腹地、后来为外来移民占据、又与新居民一同重归帝国的地方，情况也不清楚，例如保加利亚与希腊的斯拉夫人定居区（Sklabinias）。最后，还有从来不属帝国腹地、却在十世纪后期和十一世纪被吞并的外部领地，例如高加索诸公国。罗马法是否被引入这些领土？国家是否把它们的居民当作（名义上或实际上的）罗马公民对待，即便他们在文化和族群上尚未同化？在本章所讨论的时期，显然有许多人并未同化。罗马社会也许视他们在族群上有所不同，但当他们与国家正式打交道时，国家是否把他们当作罗马公民对待？

en: The basic principle of the law, quoted above, required that these people be seen as Roman citizens. In practice, however, we do not know how this played out. Small groups admitted to the empire and resettled, would, as we have seen, have been absorbed and fallen under the same legal regime as other Romans; indeed, with few exceptions, over time they became ethnic Romans as well. But the treatment of larger groups such as the Bulgarians and Armenians remains opaque. We have little evidence. In the sixth century, Justinian tried to align some “barbaric” social practices in the newly annexed Armenian territories (e.g., regarding inheritances) with Roman norms, proclaiming that Armenia should not have different laws from the rest of the Roman state, a statement that implies an intention of universal legal homogenization on his part.
According to the ideology of his regime, moreover, barbarians brought within the orbit of the empire had to be civilized, converted, and assimilated to Roman norms.

In time, this could have made them into Roman citizens indistinguishable from others across the empire. But we do not know the extent to which such a global program was implemented or enforced, what its impact was on daily life in the new provinces, or whether it was accompanied by reforms in areas beyond inheritance and (inevitably) taxation and recruitment.
zh: 上文所引的法律基本原则要求把这些人视为罗马公民。然而在实践中，我们不知道这是如何落实的。如前所见，被接纳进帝国并重新安置的小群体，会融入当地人口，和其他罗马人一样受同一套法律管辖；的确，除少数例外，随着时间推移他们也成了族群意义上的罗马人。但对保加尔人和亚美尼亚人这类较大群体的待遇仍不明朗。我们证据很少。六世纪，查士丁尼试图使新吞并的亚美尼亚领土上某些“蛮族”的社会习俗（如继承习俗）符合罗马规范，宣称亚美尼亚不应有与罗马国家其余部分不同的法律，这一声明暗示他想在全境推行统一的法律规范。
此外，按照其政权的意识形态，被纳入帝国势力范围的蛮族必须被开化、改宗，并同化于罗马规范。
假以时日，这本可把他们变成与帝国各地其他人无异的罗马公民。但我们不知道这套全面的方案在多大程度上得到实施或强制执行，它对新行省的日常生活有何影响，也不知道除了继承和（不可避免的）税收与征兵之外，它是否还伴随着其他领域的改革。

en: Turning to the tenth and eleventh centuries, we have no programmatic statements advocating the legal homogenization of newly annexed territories comparable to that of Justinian in the sixth. Court writers of the middle period certainly assumed that lawful rule by Romans would make the barbarians more civilized in all respects, but they do not show us what was happening on the ground in the provinces. The penetration of Roman law surely accompanied the extension of the imperial administration to the new territories, the evidence for which we surveyed above (probably minimal when it came to the Vlachs, deeper in Bulgaria, as-yet unknown in Armenia). This process would have faced two obstacles, one pragmatic, the other religious. Pragmatically, the empire would have had to tolerate the customs, norms, and even laws of its new subjects, at least initially, since it was not possible to change them overnight, or even in the long term. There was precedent for this. The Latin-Lombard population of the southern Italian provinces lived under its own laws, upon which the imperial administration was superimposed. It is likely that the Vlachs of Mt. Pindos, the Albanians further north, and the Milengoi on Mt. Taygetos also lived under conditions of quasi-autonomy, beyond providing tribute and soldiers to the empire. The Varangians had their own corps-code. Also, Basileios II initially allowed the Bulgarians to continue living under their own “customs,” though the exact legal implications of this rather general statement are unclear.

We do not know what Bulgarian law looked like, and the Bulgarians would in any case have been subject to Orthodox canon law, which was entangled with imperial law on multiple levels. But there was room within the empire for local “custom” as a sublegal norm.
zh: 转到十、十一世纪，我们没有看到可与六世纪查士丁尼相媲美的、主张在新吞并的领土上推行统一法律的纲领性声明。中期的宫廷作家当然假定，罗马人施行法治会使蛮族在各方面都更加开化，但他们没有向我们展示行省实地正在发生什么。罗马法的渗透无疑伴随着帝国行政机构向新领土的延伸，关于后者的证据我们已在上文考察过（就弗拉赫人而言可能微乎其微，在保加利亚较深，在亚美尼亚则尚不可知）。这一过程会面临两个障碍，一个来自实际治理，另一个来自宗教。就实际治理而言，帝国至少起初不得不宽容其新臣民的习俗、规范甚至法律，因为不可能一夜之间改变它们，甚至长期内也做不到。这方面有先例。南意大利各行省的拉丁—伦巴第居民仍沿用自己的法律，帝国在此基础上建立行政管理。品都斯山的弗拉赫人、更北面的阿尔巴尼亚人，以及泰格托斯山的米伦戈伊人，很可能也享有准自治，只须向帝国缴纳贡赋、提供兵员。瓦良格人有自己的军团法典。此外，瓦西里二世起初允许保加尔人继续沿用自己的“习俗”，尽管这一相当笼统的声明的确切法律含义尚不清楚。
我们不知道保加利亚法律是什么样子，但无论如何，保加尔人须遵守正教教会法，而教会法与帝国法律在多个层面相互交织。地方“习俗”在帝国内仍有容身之处，只是效力低于正式法律。

en: This brings us to religious limitations on legal homogeneity. Whereas late Roman law had effectively eliminated distinctions among the
and

of the empire, starting in the fourth century it re-created a new set of distinctions based on doctrinal affiliation: full rights were enjoyed by those who adhered to the doctrine preferred by the imperial authorities, while all others suffered under various degrees of legal discrimination.

Heresy was defined as a quasi-criminal act that potentially carried severe legal consequences. As communities coalesced around deviant doctrines in the fifth and centuries, these laws alienated them from Constantinople. Thus, the former Roman distinction between conquerors and conquered was replaced by that between the Orthodox Romans and others, the latter including pagans, Jews, and Christian heretics. In theory, one could not enjoy the full rights of Roman citizenship without being Orthodox.
zh: 宗教也限制了法律的统一。晚期罗马法实际上已消除了帝国各
（族群）与
（城市共同体）之间的区分，但从四世纪起，它又依照人们所信奉的教义划出新的界限：凡信奉帝国当局所偏好教义者享有完整权利，其余所有人则遭受不同程度的法律歧视。
异端被界定为一种准犯罪行为，可能带来严重的法律后果。自五世纪起，信奉不同教义的群体逐渐凝聚成形，这些法律使他们疏远君士坦丁堡。［校注：底本在第五世纪之后缺词，无法确定所指年代的上限。］于是，罗马人从前那种征服者与被征服者之间的区分，被正教罗马人与其他人之间的区分所取代，后者包括异教徒、犹太人和被视为异端的基督徒。理论上，一个人若非正教徒，便不能享有罗马公民身份的完整权利。

en: Thus, specific categories of imperial subjects would have remained under a differentiated system of law. Jews were in some respects treated as Romans, in other areas their rights were curtailed, and beyond that, as non-Christians, they would have been subject to the authority of their own religious leadership. The Muslim communities that lived in the empire after the age of the great conquests were probably subject to the jurisdiction of their

except when they entered into legal disputes with Romans. It would have been difficult, if not impossible, to integrate Muslims into the Roman legal system by this point. Turning to the Syrian Jacobites, imperial law would have classified them as heretics of some kind. As we saw, however, the imperial authorities and other Romans in Syria were apparently willing to treat the Jacobites as full Roman citizens with equal rights (intermarrying with them, accepting them as equals in court, etc.). This elicited protests by the Church, which demanded that the Jacobites be subjected to the restrictions codified in the antiheretical laws of the earlier period. But when the state cracked down on the Jacobites, it targeted only their leadership. Thus, legal distinctions based on religious differences were blurred in this case. The Roman authorities do not seem to have used the law to enforce differences to the full extent that they could. To the contrary, the state (as opposed to the Church) appears to have been willing to overlook religious differences for the purposes of legal and administrative convenience. Even some non-Chalcedonian Armenians were appointed to high office.
zh: 因此，帝国的一些臣民在法律上仍会受到区别对待。犹太人在某些方面被当作罗马人对待，在另一些领域其权利受到限制，除此之外，作为非基督徒，他们还要服从自己宗教领导层的权威。大征服时代之后生活在帝国境内的穆斯林共同体，大概服从其

（qadis）的司法管辖，除非他们与罗马人发生法律纠纷。到这时，要把穆斯林纳入罗马法体系，恐怕已极为困难，甚至根本办不到。转到叙利亚雅各派，帝国法律会把他们归为某种异端。然而如前所见，叙利亚的帝国当局和其他罗马人显然愿意把雅各派当作享有平等权利的完整罗马公民对待（与他们通婚、在法庭上给予他们平等待遇，等等）。这引来了教会的抗议，教会要求对雅各派施行早期反异端法律规定的限制。但当国家打击雅各派时，它只针对其领导层。因此，在这个案例中，基于宗教差异的法律区分被模糊了。罗马当局似乎并未把法律规定的差别待遇施行到底。恰恰相反，国家（与教会相对）似乎愿意为了法律与行政上的便利而忽略宗教差异。甚至有些非卡尔西顿派的亚美尼亚人也获任要职。

en: It is also possible that, long before the conquests, Roman law had already influenced the legal traditions of the Bulgarians, Armenians, Georgians, Syrians, and Melkites, thereby smoothing the interface between them and the imperial administration in the eleventh century. This avenue for homogenization is an area that deserves more attention.

On the other hand, law could go only so far in structuring how the Romans governed their non-Roman subjects. Perceptions of ethnic difference did not necessarily follow legal definitions. Orthodox Slavs, Bulgarians, Armenians, and Georgians who lived in the empire and were subject to some kind of Roman law were still viewed as ethnically different from the Romans on the basis of traits that were invisible to the law. Even without a strict legal basis, these differences could result in state policies and social attitudes with real consequences. There is evidence that the Roman state treated its non-Roman subjects differently, albeit not on the basis of explicit legal distinctions. This is another area where ethnicity and empire intersected.
zh: 也有可能，早在征服之前，罗马法就已经影响了保加尔人、亚美尼亚人、格鲁吉亚人、叙利亚人和麦尔基派的法律传统，让他们在十一世纪更容易与帝国行政当局往来。这也是法律逐渐趋同的一条途径，值得进一步研究。

另一方面，法律在塑造罗马人如何治理其非罗马臣民方面，作用终究有限。对族群差异的感知未必遵循法律定义。在帝国境内，即使同为正教徒并在某种程度上受罗马法管辖，斯拉夫人、保加尔人、亚美尼亚人和格鲁吉亚人仍被罗马人凭法律并不承认的特征视为异族。即便没有严格的法律依据，这些差异也能导致具有实际后果的国家政策和社会态度。有证据表明，罗马国家对其非罗马臣民区别对待，尽管并非基于明确的法律区分。这是族群与帝国交汇的又一个领域。

en: Romans of the eleventh century were certainly aware that they were living in a diverse, expansive state. Yet the only place where they expressed satisfaction about this new state of affairs was in imperial orations, where they praised the emperor for ruling over so many nations. Otherwise, when they came face to face with this diversity they did not like it, which was another reason why the literary elite preferred to stay in Constantinople if they could. Eustathios Boïlas complained when he had to leave his native land, Orthodox Cappadocia, and go settle, still within the empire, “among alien nations with a strange religion and tongue,” that is, Armenians.
The monastic founder Nikon of the Black Mountain who settled near Antioch demonstrated his Orthodox faith by stating that he had received it “from his ancestors; these were
people who had been raised and lived in any of the places and lands where the heresies are all mixed up together, but were a Roman root, via the grace of Christ.”
Being Roman functioned for him as a marker of Orthodoxy.
zh: 十一世纪的罗马人当然意识到自己生活在一个幅员辽阔且多族群的国家里。然而，只有在献给皇帝的颂辞中，他们才为出现这种局面而欣喜，赞美皇帝统治着如此众多的民族。除此之外，当他们直面这种多样性时，他们并不喜欢它，这也是文学精英只要可能就宁愿留在君士坦丁堡的另一个原因。欧斯塔提奥斯·博伊拉斯不得不离开信奉正教的故乡卡帕多基亚时，便抱怨说，虽仍住在帝国境内，却要生活“在宗教与语言都陌生的异族之间”，也就是亚美尼亚人中间。
定居在安条克附近的修道院创建者黑山的尼孔，以出身证明自己信奉正教，表示这一信仰“承自他的祖先。他们
在异端混杂之地长大或生活的人，而是蒙基督恩典，出自罗马的根脉”。
对他而言，身为罗马人起到了正教标志的作用。

en: When the historian Michael Attaleiates sought to explain the empire’s many defeats in the later eleventh century, he began by refuting the religious explanations given by the pious. To explain why so many of those who lived under Roman authority were being cut down by the Turks, they supposed at first that the Armenians and Jacobites were paying the price for their impiety. But then the troubles reached the Orthodox too, and the Romans did not know what to make of it.

This reveals that the Romans placed their non-Orthodox subjects into a different moral category from themselves, even when it came to foreign attacks against their own empire. It revealed also that distinctions had become muddled. As Psellos put it in a letter: “Romanity and barbarity are no longer clearly distinguished, but are all mixed up together.”
Needless to say, he was not celebrating its greater diversity. He was referring to foreign barbarians who were invading the empire, not to its ethnic subjects.
zh: 当历史学家米海尔·阿塔雷阿特斯试图解释帝国在十一世纪后期的诸多败绩时，他首先驳斥了虔信者给出的宗教解释。为了解释为何那么多身处罗马治下的人被突厥人杀戮，他们起先说，是亚美尼亚人和雅各派因不虔敬而受罚。但随后灾祸也降临到正教徒身上，罗马人便不知如何理解了。
这表明，罗马人把其非正教臣民归入一个与自己不同的道德范畴，即便涉及的是外敌对他们自己帝国的攻击。这也表明，以往的界限已经模糊。正如普塞洛斯在一封信中所说：“罗马性与蛮族性不再清晰可分，而是全都混杂在一起。”
不消说，他并不是在颂扬帝国更大的多样性。他指的是入侵帝国的外族蛮人，而非帝国内部的少数族群臣民。

en: The empire seems to have exerted minimal or almost no institutional or infrastructural control over certain groups in mountainous areas, such as the Vlachs and Albanians. Unfortunately, the evidence is scanty and does not extend to the crucial details, but it points to a loose relationship mediated by local ethnic leaders who interfaced with the imperial authorities. Both groups were capable of raiding imperial territories or striking deals with foreign invaders, but in times of peace they did owe the empire soldiers and tribute. This loose arrangement had a precedent in the empire’s relationship with the Ezerites and Milengoi in the Peloponnese, who were ruled by their own ethnic

Religious groups, as we have seen in the case of the Jews, Muslims, and Jacobites, were also treated as “others” in some ways or in some contexts, for example in having their own religious authorities and their own “laws”; in being occasionally persecuted by the imperial Church; and so on.
zh: 帝国似乎对山区某些群体——例如弗拉赫人和阿尔巴尼亚人——借助制度或基础设施所能施行的管控甚少，甚至几乎没有。遗憾的是，证据稀少，且缺乏关键细节，但看来他们与帝国的关系相当松散，由当地族群首领出面与帝国当局往来。这两个群体都有能力袭扰帝国领土，或与外敌入侵者达成协议，但在和平时期他们确有义务向帝国提供兵员和贡赋。这种松散安排有先例，即帝国与伯罗奔尼撒的埃泽里特斯人和米伦戈伊人的关系，这两个群体由各自的族群
（archons）统治。如我们在犹太人、穆斯林和雅各派的案例中所见，宗教群体在某些方面或某些语境下也被当作“他者”对待，例如拥有自己的宗教当局和自己的“法律”；偶尔受到帝国教会的迫害；等等。

en: There is another criterion that demonstrates clearly that the state treated these minorities differently from the way it treated Romans: there is no evidence of Jacobite, Jewish, and Muslim subjects of the empire receiving court titles and offices and placed in command positions (unlike what happened with select Armenians and Bulgarians). This discrimination effectively made these groups into a third-class category of subjects (the Armenians and Bulgarians being second-class).
zh: 从授官情况也可清楚看出，国家对待这些少数群体的方式不同于对待罗马人：没有证据显示帝国的雅各派、犹太人和穆斯林臣民获得宫廷头衔、官职或指挥权，少数亚美尼亚人和保加尔人却有这样的例子。这种歧视实际上使这些群体沦为第三等臣民（亚美尼亚人和保加尔人则为第二等）。

en: Turning from people and cultures to geography, the Byzantine state in the eleventh century exhibits the hub-and-spoke image of segmented empires. The Vlach, Albanian, and Bulgarian subjects in the European provinces were linked to each other through proximity and history and to the imperial capital but not to the Georgian, Armenian, and Syrian subjects of the Asian provinces. Here the empire’s fundamental geographical feature, the fact that it was divided into two by the sea, played a fundamental role in allowing it to keep its holdings isolated from each other and segmented. It was also advantageous that the capital was so situated as to control the narrowest point of passage from one continent to the other, the Bosporos. Therefore, the Vlachs could collaborate with Bulgarians, and eventually did so, when they jointly broke away from the empire in 1185, and the Armenians could collaborate with the Syrians, but the empire’s two halves were largely independent worlds, linked only through Constantinople. The Adriatic functioned in a similar way for the Italian provinces. Even when they were lost to foreign invaders, the Normans, the latter ultimately proved unable to expand to the empire’s core Balkan territories.
zh: 从人群与文化转向地理，十一世纪的拜占庭国家呈现出分区治理的帝国所具有的轮毂—辐条结构。欧洲行省的弗拉赫人、阿尔巴尼亚人和保加尔人因地理邻近和历史联系彼此往来。他们都与帝国都城有联系，同亚洲行省的格鲁吉亚人、亚美尼亚人和叙利亚人却没有往来。海洋将帝国一分为二，对维持各片领地间的区隔至关重要。同样有利的是，都城所处的位置恰好控制着从一块大陆通往另一块大陆的最窄通道，即博斯普鲁斯海峡（Bosporos）。因此，弗拉赫人与保加尔人可以合作，并于1185年合力脱离帝国，亚美尼亚人也可以与叙利亚人合作。不过，帝国的东西两半大体各成一体，只靠君士坦丁堡相连。亚得里亚海对意大利行省起了类似的作用。即使诺曼人夺取了这些行省，最终也没能将势力扩张到帝国在巴尔干的核心领土。

en: Let us consider also the distinction posed at the beginning of Chapter 6: looking at Romanía as an empire, should we say that it
an empire or that it
an empire? To the extent that it may be understood as an empire at all, the answer is clearly that Romanía

an empire. It was a core national state, Romanía or “Romanland,” that at times acquired territories or ethnic subjects whom it governed in an imperial way. Romanía existed before, during, and after those acquisitions. It lost the east after 1071 and it lost Bulgaria in 1185, but it still retained its own identity. It was always the
of the Romans plus their
over non-Romans, whether the latter was larger or smaller.

一个帝国，还是说它
一个帝国？如果一定要用帝国来理解它，答案显然是：罗曼尼亚
一个帝国。作为核心民族国家，罗曼尼亚即“罗马之地”，有时取得新的领土和族群臣民，以帝国的方式治理他们。无论在扩张之前、扩张过程中还是扩张之后，罗曼尼亚都继续存在。它在1071年后失去了东方，在1185年失去了保加利亚，但它依然保持自身的政治身份。它始终是罗马人的
（政治共同体），加上他们对非罗马人的
（统治权），无论后者是大是小。

en: Around 1064 the empire was marked by a higher degree of ethnic and religious diversity than at any point in the previous four centuries. Many of its new ethnic subjects expressed their distinctiveness through narratives in Latin, Hebrew, Slavonic, Armenian, Syriac, and Arabic. These works foregrounded these communities’ separate experience of those two centuries. One day they might be studied together as comparable products of the Byzantine imperial periphery, rather than segregated, as they are today, into siloed fields defined by linguistic training, nationality, or religious confession.
zh: 约1064年，帝国的族群与宗教多样性程度，高于此前四百年间的任何时候。它的许多新族群臣民通过拉丁语、希伯来语、斯拉夫语、亚美尼亚语、叙利亚语和阿拉伯语的叙事来表达自身的独特性。这些作品突出各个社群在十至十一世纪各自的经历。有朝一日，它们或许会被放在一起研究，作为拜占庭帝国边缘地区的作品相互比较。时至今日，它们仍分属不同领域，因研究者所习语言、作品的民族归属或宗教派别而彼此分开。

en: The majority of the population of the empire always remained Roman. This was unlike most empires, in which the ruling ethnic group is a minority. Moreover, the default setting of the Roman state in this phase of its expansion was, wherever possible, to homogenize its administration of conquered territories, even to the degree of disregarding religious differences that would otherwise produce radically unequal subject populations. Islam could not, of course, be overlooked in this way, but the anti-Chalcedonian otherness of the Jacobites and Armenians was accommodated, up to a point. Hence it could justly be said by a court orator in the 1040s that “New Rome ruled over many nations
zh: 帝国人口的多数始终是罗马人。这不同于大多数帝国——在那些帝国里，统治族群是少数。此外，罗马国家在这一扩张阶段通常尽可能让被征服地区采用一致的行政制度，甚至不计较宗教差异，否则信仰不同的臣民在地位上本会悬殊。当然，伊斯兰教无法如此通融，但帝国在一定程度上接纳了坚持反卡尔西顿立场的雅各派和亚美尼亚人。因此，1040年代一位宫廷演说家有理由说：“新罗马统治着许多民族（

en: It has been said that “in losing its frontiers and opening itself to the world, it is a bit as if Byzantium had lost its definition.”

We might reformulate this and say that it had become a bit less like a nation-state and a bit more like an empire, however briefly. Whether the balance swung categorically from the former type of state to the latter is an artificial question. Overall, “Byzantium” was not really an empire. In terms of population, geography, and political orientation, it was overwhelmingly the ethnic or national state of the Romans, their “polity,” as they called it, which at various times exercised a looser or tighter hegemony over non-Romans: Romanía
an empire, or rather it entered into imperial relationships at times with conquered subjects along the margins, but its own essence was not that of an empire.
zh: 有人说：“拜占庭失去边疆、向外部世界开放，仿佛也有些失去了自身的界定。”
换一种说法，在那短暂的时期，它稍稍离民族国家远了一点，离帝国近了一点。硬要追问天平是否彻底从一种国家形态倒向另一种，是人为设下的问题。总的来说，“拜占庭”并不真正是一个帝国。就人口、地理和政治取向而言，它主要是罗马人的族群国家或民族国家，也就是他们所说的“政治共同体”，在不同时期对非罗马人行使或强或弱的支配权。罗曼尼亚

en: Matthew of Edessa,
2.30 (the sermon follows), 2.42–43; see 1.77 for a hagiography of Gagik. For skepticism, see Cheynet,

401–402; “Arméniens,” 68–69. Matthew had no understanding of the Roman centralized state and intuitively viewed history through the lens of Armenian “feudal” relations, so he gives the impression that the royals were ruling their own domains. He sometimes makes it seem as if they brought their royal sovereignty to their Byzantine possessions (1.54, 1.62), although he knows they followed the emperor’s orders (1.80). The problem extends to a propensity for tall tales that cannot be taken at face value, as scholars have recognized. When his account can be checked against sober or contemporary sources, he often fails. For some examples regarding the tenth century, see Kaldellis, “Did Ioannes I Tzimiskes Campaign in the East in 974?”
